  inp: {width:"100%",padding:"10px 14px",borderRadius:9,border:"1.5px solid #e2e8f0",fontSize:14,boxSizing:"border-box",marginBottom:10,outline:"none",fontFamily:"inherit",background:"#f8fafc"},
  ta: {width:"100%",padding:"10px 14px",borderRadius:9,border:"1.5px solid #e2e8f0",fontSize:14,boxSizing:"border-box",marginBottom:10,minHeight:110,resize:"vertical",outline:"none",fontFamily:"inherit",background:"#f8fafc"},
  card: {background:"#fff",borderRadius:14,padding:22,marginBottom:16,boxShadow:"0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.06),0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.04)"},
  chip: (on,c="#1d4ed8") => ({padding:"7px 16px",borderRadius:20,border:"2px solid " + (on?c:"#e2e8f0"),background:on?c+"18":"#fff",color:on?c:"#6b7280",cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:13,transition:"all 0.15s",fontFamily:"inherit"}),
};

// â”€â”€â”€ MARKDOWN RENDERER â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
function renderMD(text) {
  if (!text) return null;
  const lines = text.split('\n');
  const els = []; let i = 0;
  while (i < lines.length) {
    const line = lines[i];
    if (line.startsWith('## ')) {
      els.push(<h3 key={i} style={{color:'#1d4ed8',margin:'18px 0 6px',fontSize:15,fontWeight:800,borderBottom:'2px solid #dbeafe',paddingBottom:4}}>{line.slice(3)}</h3>);
      i++;
    } else if (line.startsWith('### ')) {
      els.push(<h4 key={i} style={{color:'#b91c1c',margin:'14px 0 4px',fontSize:14,fontWeight:700}}>{line.slice(4)}</h4>);
      i++;
    } else if (line.startsWith('""`')) {
      const lang = line.slice(3).trim();
      const code = [];
      i++;
      while (i < lines.length && !lines[i].startsWith('`""')) { code.push(lines[i]); i++; }
      i++;
      els.push(
        <div key={i} style={{background:'#0f172a',borderRadius:10,padding:'14px 16px',margin:'10px 0',overflowX:'auto',border:'1px solid #1e293b'}}>
          {lang && <div style={{color:'#64748b',fontSize:11,marginBottom:6,fontFamily:'monospace',textTransform:'uppercase',letterSpacing:1}}>{lang}</div>}
          <pre style={{color:'#e2e8f0',margin:0,fontSize:13,lineHeight:1.7,fontFamily:"'Fira Code','Cascadia Code','Courier New',monospace",whiteSpace:'pre-wrap'}}>{code.join('\n')}</pre>
        </div>
      );
    } else if (line.startsWith('- ') || line.startsWith('â€¢ ')) {
      const items = [];
      while (i < lines.length && (lines[i].startsWith('- ')||lines[i].startsWith('â€¢ '))) { items.push(lines[i].slice(2)); i++; }
      els.push(<ul key={i} style={{margin:'6px 0 10px',paddingLeft:20}}>{items.map((it,j)=><li key={j} style={{margin:'3px 0',lineHeight:1.6,fontSize:14}} dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html:it.replace(/\*\*(.+?)\*\*/g,'<strong>$1</strong>').replace(/"(.+?)"/g,'<code style="background:#f1f5f9;padding:1px 5px;border-radius:3px;font-size:12px;font-family:monospace">$1</code>')}}/>)}</ul>);
    } else if (line.startsWith('âœ…')||line.startsWith('âŒ')||line.startsWith('â–¡')) {
      const items = [];
      while (i < lines.length && (lines[i].startsWith('âœ…')||lines[i].startsWith('âŒ')||lines[i].startsWith('â–¡'))) { items.push(lines[i]); i++; }
      els.push(<div key={i} style={{margin:'6px 0 10px'}}>{items.map((it,j)=><div key={j} style={{margin:'4px 0',fontSize:14,lineHeight:1.6,padding:'3px 8px',background:it.startsWith('âœ…')?'#f0fdf4':it.startsWith('âŒ')?'#fef2f2':'#f8fafc',borderRadius:5}} dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html:it.replace(/\*\*(.+?)\*\*/g,'<strong>$1</strong>')}}/>)}</div>);
    } else if (line.startsWith('|')) {
      const rows = [];
      while (i < lines.length && lines[i].startsWith('|')) { if (!lines[i].match(/^\|[\s\-|]+\|$/)) rows.push(lines[i]); i++; }
      els.push(<div key={i} style={{overflowX:'auto',margin:'10px 0',borderRadius:8,border:'1px solid #e2e8f0'}}><table style={{borderCollapse:'collapse',width:'100%',fontSize:13}}>{rows.map((row,ri)=>{const cells=row.split('|').filter(c=>c.trim()!=='');return(<tr key={ri} style={{background:ri===0?'#1e40af':ri%2===0?'#f8fafc':'#fff'}}>{cells.map((c,ci)=>{const Tag=ri===0?'th':'td';return<Tag key={ci} style={{padding:'8px 12px',borderBottom:'1px solid #e2e8f0',color:ri===0?'#fff':'#374151',fontWeight:ri===0?700:400,textAlign:'left'}} dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html:c.trim().replace(/\*\*(.+?)\*\*/g,'<strong>$1</strong>')}}/>;})}</tr>);})}</table></div>);
    } else if (line.trim()==='---') {
      els.push(<hr key={i} style={{border:'none',borderTop:'2px solid #e2e8f0',margin:'14px 0'}}/>);
      i++;
    } else if (line.trim()==='') {
      els.push(<div key={i} style={{height:6}}/>);
      i++;
    } else {
      const html = line.replace(/\*\*(.+?)\*\*/g,'<strong>$1</strong>').replace(/"(.+?)"/g,'<code style="background:#f1f5f9;padding:1px 5px;border-radius:3px;font-family:monospace;font-size:12px">$1</code>');
      els.push(<p key={i} style={{margin:'3px 0 6px',lineHeight:1.7,fontSize:14}} dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html:html}}/>);
      i++;
    }
  }
  return els;
}

// â”€â”€â”€ SCENARIO LESSON RENDERER â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
function ScenarioLesson({ lesson }) {
  const [phase, setPhase] = useState("intro");
  const [scIdx, setScIdx] = useState(0);
  const [chosen, setChosen] = useState(null);
  const [revealed, setRevealed] = useState(false);

  const sc = lesson.scenarios[scIdx];
  const total = lesson.scenarios.length;

  if (phase === "intro") return (
    <div>
      <div style={{background:"linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a,#1d4ed8)",borderRadius:14,padding:22,color:"#fff",marginBottom:18}}>
        <div style={{fontSize:28,marginBottom:8}}>ðŸŽ¯ Scenario Training</div>
        <div style={{fontSize:15,opacity:0.9,lineHeight:1.6,marginBottom:16}}>{lesson.intro}</div>
        <div style={{fontSize:13,opacity:0.75}}>{total} scenario{total>1?"s":""} Â· Make decisions, see outcomes</div>
      </div>
      <button style={{background:"#1d4ed8",color:"#fff",border:"none",padding:"11px 24px",borderRadius:9,cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:14,fontFamily:"inherit"}} onClick={()=>setPhase("quiz")}>Start Scenarios â†’</button>
    </div>
  );

  if (phase === "done") return (
    <div style={{background:"linear-gradient(135deg,#166534,#16a34a)",borderRadius:14,padding:24,color:"#fff",textAlign:"center"}}>
      <div style={{fontSize:40,marginBottom:10}}>ðŸ†</div>
      <div style={{fontSize:22,fontWeight:900,marginBottom:6}}>Scenarios Complete!</div>
      <div style={{fontSize:14,opacity:0.85,marginBottom:16}}>You've worked through all {total} real FIRST decision scenarios.</div>
      <button style={{background:"rgba(255,255,255,0.2)",border:"2px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.5)",color:"#fff",padding:"9px 22px",borderRadius:8,cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:13,fontFamily:"inherit"}} onClick={()=>{setPhase("intro");setScIdx(0);setChosen(null);setRevealed(false);}}>Replay Scenarios</button>
    </div>
  );

  const choiceColors = ["#1d4ed8","#7c3aed","#b45309"];

  return (
    <div>
      <div style={{display:"flex",justifyContent:"space-between",alignItems:"center",marginBottom:14}}>
        <div style={{fontWeight:800,fontSize:15,color:"#0f172a"}}>ðŸŽ¯ Scenario {scIdx+1} of {total}</div>
        <div style={{background:"#e2e8f0",borderRadius:20,height:6,width:120,overflow:"hidden"}}>
          <div style={{background:"#1d4ed8",width:(((scIdx)/total)*100) + "%",height:"100%",borderRadius:20,transition:"width 0.4s"}}/>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div style={{background:"#fef9f0",border:"2px solid #fed7aa",borderRadius:12,padding:18,marginBottom:18}}>
        <div style={{fontWeight:700,fontSize:15,color:"#92400e",lineHeight:1.6}}>{sc.question}</div>
      </div>
      <div style={{display:"flex",flexDirection:"column",gap:10,marginBottom:16}}>
        {sc.choices.map((ch,i)=>{
          let bg="#f8fafc",border="1.5px solid #e2e8f0",col="#374151";
          if(revealed){
            if(i===sc.correct){bg="#f0fdf4";border="2px solid #86efac";col="#166534";}
            else if(chosen===i){bg="#fef2f2";border="2px solid #fca5a5";col="#991b1b";}
          } else if(chosen===i){bg=choiceColors[i%3]+"12";border="2px solid " + (choiceColors[i%3]);col=choiceColors[i%3];}
          return (
            <button key={i} onClick={()=>{if(!revealed)setChosen(i);}}
              style={{background:bg,border,color:col,padding:"12px 16px",borderRadius:10,cursor:revealed?"default":"pointer",textAlign:"left",fontWeight:chosen===i?700:500,fontSize:14,fontFamily:"inherit",transition:"all 0.15s",lineHeight:1.5}}>
              <span style={{fontWeight:800,marginRight:10}}>{String.fromCharCode(65+i)}.</span>{ch}
            </button>
          );
        })}
      </div>
      {revealed && (
        <div style={{background:chosen===sc.correct?"#f0fdf4":"#fff7ed",border:"2px solid " + (chosen===sc.correct?"#86efac":"#fed7aa"),borderRadius:10,padding:14,marginBottom:14,fontSize:14,lineHeight:1.6,color:chosen===sc.correct?"#166534":"#92400e"}}>
          <div style={{fontWeight:800,marginBottom:4}}>{chosen===sc.correct?"âœ… Good thinking!":"ðŸ’¡ Here's why:"}</div>
          {sc.outcomes[chosen]}
        </div>
      )}
      <div style={{display:"flex",gap:10}}>
        {!revealed && <button style={{background:"#1d4ed8",color:"#fff",border:"none",padding:"9px 20px",borderRadius:8,cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:14,fontFamily:"inherit",opacity:chosen===null?0.5:1}} onClick={()=>setRevealed(true)} disabled={chosen===null}>See Outcome</button>}
        {revealed && <button style={{background:"#16a34a",color:"#fff",border:"none",padding:"9px 20px",borderRadius:8,cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:14,fontFamily:"inherit"}} onClick={()=>{if(scIdx+1>=total){setPhase("done");}else{setScIdx(s=>s+1);setChosen(null);setRevealed(false);}}}>
          {scIdx+1>=total?"Finish âœ“":"Next Scenario â†’"}
        </button>}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

// â”€â”€â”€ CHECKLIST LESSON RENDERER â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
function ChecklistLesson({ lesson }) {
  const [checked, setChecked] = useState({});
  const [showTip, setShowTip] = useState(null);
  const total = lesson.items.length;
  const done = Object.values(checked).filter(Boolean).length;
  const pct = Math.round(done/total*100);

  return (
    <div>
      <div style={{background:"linear-gradient(135deg,#064e3b,#065f46)",borderRadius:14,padding:18,color:"#fff",marginBottom:18}}>
        <div style={{fontSize:13,opacity:0.8,marginBottom:4,letterSpacing:1,textTransform:"uppercase",fontWeight:700}}>âœ… Interactive Checklist</div>
        <div style={{fontSize:15,opacity:0.9,lineHeight:1.5}}>{lesson.intro}</div>
      </div>
      <div style={{display:"flex",alignItems:"center",gap:12,marginBottom:18}}>
        <div style={{flex:1,background:"#e2e8f0",borderRadius:20,height:10,overflow:"hidden"}}>
          <div style={{background:pct===100?"#16a34a":"linear-gradient(90deg,#1d4ed8,#7c3aed)",width:(pct) + "%",height:"100%",borderRadius:20,transition:"width 0.4s"}}/>
        </div>
        <div style={{fontWeight:800,fontSize:14,color:pct===100?"#16a34a":"#1d4ed8",minWidth:55}}>{done}/{total}</div>
      </div>
      <div style={{display:"flex",flexDirection:"column",gap:8}}>
        {lesson.items.map((item,i)=>{
          const isChecked = !!checked[item.id];
          const isTipOpen = showTip===item.id;
          return (
            <div key={item.id} style={{background:isChecked?"#f0fdf4":"#fff",border:"2px solid " + (isChecked?"#86efac":"#e2e8f0"),borderRadius:12,padding:"12px 14px",transition:"all 0.2s"}}>
              <div style={{display:"flex",alignItems:"flex-start",gap:12}}>
                <button onClick={()=>setChecked(p=>({...p,[item.id]:!isChecked}))}
                  style={{width:24,height:24,borderRadius:7,border:"2px solid " + (isChecked?"#16a34a":"#d1d5db"),background:isChecked?"#16a34a":"#fff",cursor:"pointer",display:"flex",alignItems:"center",justifyContent:"center",flexShrink:0,fontSize:14,transition:"all 0.2s",marginTop:1}}>
                  {isChecked && <span style={{color:"#fff",fontWeight:900}}>âœ“</span>}
                </button>
                <div style={{flex:1}}>
                  <div style={{fontSize:14,fontWeight:isChecked?700:500,color:isChecked?"#166534":"#1e293b",lineHeight:1.5,textDecoration:isChecked?"line-through":"none",textDecorationColor:"#86efac"}}>
                    {i+1}. {item.text}
                  </div>
                  {isTipOpen && (
                    <div style={{background:"#fffbeb",border:"1px solid #fde68a",borderRadius:8,padding:"8px 12px",marginTop:8,fontSize:13,color:"#92400e",lineHeight:1.5}}>
                      ðŸ’¡ {item.tip}
                    </div>
                  )}
                </div>
                <button onClick={()=>setShowTip(isTipOpen?null:item.id)}
                  style={{background:isTipOpen?"#fef3c7":"#f1f5f9",border:"none",borderRadius:6,padding:"3px 8px",cursor:"pointer",fontSize:12,fontWeight:700,color:isTipOpen?"#b45309":"#6b7280",flexShrink:0}}>
                  {isTipOpen?"âœ•":"ðŸ’¡"}
                </button>
              </div>
            </div>
          );
        })}
      </div>
      {pct===100 && (
        <div style={{background:"linear-gradient(135deg,#166534,#16a34a)",borderRadius:12,padding:16,color:"#fff",textAlign:"center",marginTop:16}}>
          <div style={{fontSize:28,marginBottom:6}}>ðŸŽ‰</div>
          <div style={{fontWeight:800,fontSize:16}}>Checklist Complete!</div>
          <div style={{fontSize:13,opacity:0.85,marginTop:4}}>All {total} items verified. You're ready.</div>
        </div>
      )}
      {done > 0 && done < total && (
        <button onClick={()=>setChecked({})} style={{background:"none",border:"none",color:"#9ca3af",fontSize:12,cursor:"pointer",textDecoration:"underline",marginTop:12,fontFamily:"inherit"}}>Reset checklist</button>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

// â”€â”€â”€ CHALLENGE LESSON RENDERER â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
function ChallengeLesson({ lesson }) {
  const [phase, setPhase] = useState("bug"); // bug | hint | fixed
  return (
    <div>
      <div style={{background:"linear-gradient(135deg,#3b0764,#7c3aed)",borderRadius:14,padding:18,color:"#fff",marginBottom:18}}>
        <div style={{fontSize:13,opacity:0.8,marginBottom:4,letterSpacing:1,textTransform:"uppercase",fontWeight:700}}>ðŸ› Debug Challenge</div>
        <div style={{fontSize:14,opacity:0.9,lineHeight:1.5}}>Find and fix all the bugs in the code below. Try before looking at hints!</div>
      </div>
      <div style={{display:"flex",gap:8,marginBottom:14}}>
        {[["bug","ðŸ› Buggy Code"],["hint","ðŸ’¡ Hint"],["fixed","âœ… Fixed Code"]].map(([p,label])=>(
          <button key={p} onClick={()=>setPhase(p)}
            style={{background:phase===p?{bug:"#7c3aed",hint:"#b45309",fixed:"#16a34a"}[p]:"#f1f5f9",color:phase===p?"#fff":"#6b7280",border:"none",padding:"8px 16px",borderRadius:8,cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:13,fontFamily:"inherit",transition:"all 0.2s"}}>
            {label}
          </button>
        ))}
      </div>
      {phase==="bug" && (
        <div>
          <div style={{background:"#0f172a",borderRadius:12,padding:16,border:"2px solid #dc2626"}}>
            <div style={{color:"#ef4444",fontSize:11,fontFamily:"monospace",marginBottom:6,letterSpacing:1,textTransform:"uppercase",fontWeight:700}}>âš  Contains {(lesson.buggedCode.match(/\/\/ BUG/g)||[]).length} known bugs â€” find them!</div>
            <pre style={{color:"#e2e8f0",margin:0,fontSize:12,lineHeight:1.8,fontFamily:"'Fira Code','Courier New',monospace",whiteSpace:"pre-wrap",overflow:"auto"}}>{lesson.buggedCode}</pre>
          </div>
          <div style={{marginTop:10,color:"#6b7280",fontSize:13}}>Spotted the bugs? Click <b>Hint</b> for a clue or <b>Fixed Code</b> to see all fixes.</div>
        </div>
      )}
      {phase==="hint" && (
        <div style={{background:"#fffbeb",border:"2px solid #fde68a",borderRadius:12,padding:18}}>
          <div style={{fontWeight:800,fontSize:14,color:"#92400e",marginBottom:8}}>ðŸ’¡ Hint (without giving it away)</div>
          <div style={{fontSize:14,color:"#78350f",lineHeight:1.6}}>{lesson.hint}</div>
        </div>
      )}
      {phase==="fixed" && (
        <div>
          <div style={{background:"#0f172a",borderRadius:12,padding:16,border:"2px solid #16a34a"}}>
            <div style={{color:"#4ade80",fontSize:11,fontFamily:"monospace",marginBottom:6,letterSpacing:1,textTransform:"uppercase",fontWeight:700}}>âœ… Fixed version â€” compare carefully</div>
            <pre style={{color:"#e2e8f0",margin:0,fontSize:12,lineHeight:1.8,fontFamily:"'Fira Code','Courier New',monospace",whiteSpace:"pre-wrap",overflow:"auto"}}>{lesson.fixedCode}</pre>
          </div>
          <div style={{background:"#f0fdf4",border:"1px solid #86efac",borderRadius:10,padding:14,marginTop:12}}>
            <div style={{fontWeight:800,fontSize:13,color:"#166534",marginBottom:6}}>ðŸ“‹ Explanation</div>
            <div style={{fontSize:14,color:"#166534",lineHeight:1.6}}>{lesson.explanation}</div>
          </div>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

// â”€â”€â”€ MATCHING LESSON â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
function MatchingLesson({ lesson }) {
  const [leftSel, setLeftSel] = useState(null);
  const [rightSel, setRightSel] = useState(null);
  const [matched, setMatched] = useState({});
  const [wrong, setWrong] = useState(null);
  const [done, setDone] = useState(false);
  const pairs = lesson.pairs || [];
  const shuffled = useRef(shuffleArr(pairs.map(p=>p.right))).current;

  function selectLeft(i) {
    if (matched[i]) return;
    setLeftSel(i); setWrong(null);
  }
  function selectRight(val) {
    if (Object.values(matched).includes(val)) return;
    if (leftSel === null) return;
    const correct = pairs[leftSel].right;
    if (val === correct) {
      const nm = {...matched, [leftSel]: val};
      setMatched(nm);
      setLeftSel(null); setRightSel(null); setWrong(null);
      if (Object.keys(nm).length === pairs.length) setDone(true);
    } else {
      setWrong(val);
      setTimeout(()=>{ setWrong(null); setLeftSel(null); }, 900);
    }
  }
  function reset() { setLeftSel(null); setRightSel(null); setMatched({}); setWrong(null); setDone(false); }

  return (
    <div style={{fontFamily:"inherit"}}>
      <div style={{fontSize:13,color:"#64748b",marginBottom:16}}>{lesson.intro||"Match each item on the left to its corresponding term on the right."}</div>
      {done ? (
        <div style={{background:"linear-gradient(135deg,#10b981,#059669)",borderRadius:16,padding:"28px 24px",textAlign:"center",color:"#fff"}}>
          <div style={{fontSize:36,marginBottom:8}}>ðŸŽ‰</div>
          <div style={{fontSize:20,fontWeight:800,marginBottom:6}}>Perfect Match!</div>
          <div style={{opacity:0.85,marginBottom:16}}>You matched all {pairs.length} pairs correctly.</div>
          <button onClick={reset} style={{background:"rgba(255,255,255,0.2)",color:"#fff",border:"2px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.4)",borderRadius:8,padding:"10px 22px",cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700}}>Try Again</button>
        </div>
      ) : (
        <div>
          <div style={{display:"grid",gridTemplateColumns:"1fr 1fr",gap:12}}>
            <div style={{display:"flex",flexDirection:"column",gap:8}}>
              <div style={{fontSize:11,fontWeight:700,color:"#94a3b8",textTransform:"uppercase",letterSpacing:1,marginBottom:4}}>Concepts</div>
              {pairs.map((p,i)=>{
                const isMatched = matched[i]!==undefined;
                const isSel = leftSel===i;
                return (
                  <div key={i} onClick={()=>selectLeft(i)}
                    style={{padding:"12px 16px",borderRadius:10,border:"2px solid " + (isMatched?"#10b981":isSel?"#1d4ed8":"#e2e8f0"),
                      background:isMatched?"#f0fdf4":isSel?"#eff6ff":"#fff",cursor:isMatched?"default":"pointer",
                      fontWeight:600,fontSize:14,color:isMatched?"#065f46":isSel?"#1e40af":"#1e293b",
                      transition:"all 0.15s",opacity:isMatched?0.7:1}}>
                    {isMatched ? <span style={{fontSize:12,color:"#10b981",marginRight:6}}>âœ“</span> : null}
                    {p.left}
                  </div>
                );
              })}
            </div>
            <div style={{display:"flex",flexDirection:"column",gap:8}}>
              <div style={{fontSize:11,fontWeight:700,color:"#94a3b8",textTransform:"uppercase",letterSpacing:1,marginBottom:4}}>Definitions</div>
              {shuffled.map((val,i)=>{
                const isMatched = Object.values(matched).includes(val);
                const isWrong = wrong===val;
                return (
                  <div key={i} onClick={()=>selectRight(val)}
                    style={{padding:"12px 16px",borderRadius:10,border:"2px solid " + (isMatched?"#10b981":isWrong?"#ef4444":leftSel!==null&&!isMatched?"#e2e8f0":"#e2e8f0"),
                      background:isMatched?"#f0fdf4":isWrong?"#fef2f2":leftSel!==null&&!isMatched?"#f8fafc":"#fff",
                      cursor:isMatched?"default":"pointer",fontSize:13,color:isMatched?"#065f46":"#334155",
                      transition:"all 0.15s",animation:isWrong?"shake 0.3s":"none",opacity:isMatched?0.7:1,lineHeight:1.4}}>
                    {isMatched ? <span style={{fontSize:12,color:"#10b981",marginRight:6}}>âœ“</span> : null}
                    {val}
                  </div>
                );
              })}
            </div>
          </div>
          <div style={{marginTop:14,display:"flex",alignItems:"center",gap:12}}>
            <div style={{flex:1,background:"#e2e8f0",borderRadius:999,height:6}}>
              <div style={{width:((Object.keys(matched).length/pairs.length)*100) + "%",background:"#10b981",height:"100%",borderRadius:999,transition:"width 0.3s"}}></div>
            </div>
            <span style={{fontSize:12,color:"#64748b"}}>{Object.keys(matched).length}/{pairs.length} matched</span>
            <button onClick={reset} style={{background:"none",border:"1px solid #e2e8f0",borderRadius:7,padding:"6px 12px",cursor:"pointer",fontSize:12,color:"#64748b"}}>Reset</button>
          </div>
          {leftSel!==null && <div style={{marginTop:10,fontSize:13,color:"#1d4ed8",fontStyle:"italic"}}>ðŸ‘† Now click a definition on the right to match with "{pairs[leftSel].left}"</div>}
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

// â”€â”€â”€ FILL-IN-THE-BLANK LESSON â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
function FillBlankLesson({ lesson }) {
  const blanks = lesson.blanks || [];
  const [answers, setAnswers] = useState(blanks.map(()=>""));
  const [checked, setChecked] = useState(false);
  const [showAll, setShowAll] = useState(false);
  const score = blanks.filter((b,i)=>answers[i].trim().toLowerCase()===b.answer.toLowerCase()).length;

  function check() { setChecked(true); }
  function reset() { setAnswers(blanks.map(()=>"")); setChecked(false); setShowAll(false); }

  return (
    <div style={{fontFamily:"inherit"}}>
      <div style={{fontSize:13,color:"#64748b",marginBottom:16}}>{lesson.intro||"Fill in the blanks to complete the code or definition."}</div>
      {blanks.map((b,i)=>{
        const isCorrect = checked && answers[i].trim().toLowerCase()===b.answer.toLowerCase();
        const isWrong = checked && answers[i].trim()!=="" && !isCorrect;
        const isEmpty = checked && answers[i].trim()==="";
        return (
          <div key={i} style={{marginBottom:18,background:"#f8fafc",borderRadius:12,padding:"16px 18px",border:"1px solid #e2e8f0"}}>
            <div style={{fontSize:13,color:"#475569",marginBottom:10,lineHeight:1.6}} dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html:b.prompt.replace("___","<span style='display:inline-block;background:#e0e7ff;padding:1px 18px;border-radius:5px;margin:0 4px;font-style:italic;color:#3730a3'>___</span>")}}/>
            {b.code && <pre style={{background:"#1e293b",color:"#e2e8f0",padding:"12px 16px",borderRadius:8,fontSize:12,marginBottom:10,overflowX:"auto",lineHeight:1.6}}>{b.code}</pre>}
            <div style={{display:"flex",alignItems:"center",gap:10}}>
              <input
                value={showAll?b.answer:answers[i]}
                onChange={e=>{ if(!checked&&!showAll){const a=[...answers];a[i]=e.target.value;setAnswers(a);}}}
                placeholder="Type your answerâ€¦"
                style={{flex:1,padding:"10px 14px",borderRadius:8,border:"2px solid " + (isCorrect?"#10b981":isWrong?"#ef4444":isEmpty?"#f59e0b":"#e2e8f0"),
                  fontSize:14,fontFamily:"'Consolas','Courier New',monospace",background:isCorrect?"#f0fdf4":isWrong?"#fef2f2":"#fff",
                  color:"#1e293b",outline:"none"}}
              />
              {checked && (
                <span style={{fontSize:18}}>{isCorrect?"âœ…":isEmpty?"âš ï¸":"âŒ"}</span>
              )}
            </div>
            {checked && !isCorrect && <div style={{marginTop:6,fontSize:12,color:"#64748b"}}>Answer: <code style={{background:"#e0e7ff",padding:"2px 8px",borderRadius:4,color:"#3730a3"}}>{b.answer}</code> â€” {b.explanation}</div>}
          </div>
        );
      })}
      <div style={{display:"flex",gap:10,marginTop:4,flexWrap:"wrap",alignItems:"center"}}>
        {!checked ? (
          <button onClick={check} style={{background:"#1d4ed8",color:"#fff",border:"none",borderRadius:8,padding:"11px 24px",cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:14}}>Check Answers</button>
        ) : (
          <>
            <div style={{background:score===blanks.length?"#10b981":score>=blanks.length/2?"#f59e0b":"#ef4444",color:"#fff",borderRadius:8,padding:"10px 18px",fontWeight:700,fontSize:15}}>
              {score}/{blanks.length} correct
            </div>
            <button onClick={reset} style={{background:"#f1f5f9",color:"#475569",border:"1px solid #e2e8f0",borderRadius:8,padding:"10px 18px",cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:600}}>Try Again</button>
            {!showAll && <button onClick={()=>setShowAll(true)} style={{background:"none",color:"#6366f1",border:"none",cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:600,fontSize:13,textDecoration:"underline"}}>Show All Answers</button>}
          </>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

// â”€â”€â”€ FLASHCARD DATA â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
const FLASHCARD_DECKS = {

  // â”€â”€â”€ 1. JAVA & FTC PROGRAMMING â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  java: {
    name: "Java & FTC Programming",
    icon: "â˜•",
    color: "#b45309",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"What does @TeleOp annotate?", a:"A class extending LinearOpMode or OpMode used for driver-controlled operation during the TeleOp phase.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What does @Autonomous annotate?", a:"A class run during the 15-second autonomous period â€” no driver input is allowed.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a LinearOpMode?", a:"An OpMode running sequentially in a single runOpMode() thread; call waitForStart() then run code top to bottom.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What does hardwareMap.get() do?", a:"Retrieves a hardware device (motor, servo, sensor) by the name configured in the Robot Controller config file.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What does motor.setPower() accept?", a:"A double from -1.0 to +1.0. -1 is full reverse, 0 is stop, +1 is full forward.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is telemetry.addData()?", a:"Sends key-value data to the Driver Station display for real-time debugging and monitoring during matches.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"Servo vs CRServo?", a:"Servo moves to a position (0.0â€“1.0). CRServo spins continuously with power (-1.0 to +1.0). Use Servo for arms, CRServo for intake rollers.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What does opModeIsActive() return?", a:"True if the OpMode is still running. Use as a while-loop condition in autonomous to handle DS stop gracefully.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a Gamepad in FTC?", a:"gamepad1/gamepad2 expose buttons (.a, .b, .x, .y), joysticks (.left_stick_x/y), and triggers (.left_trigger).", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is DcMotor.Direction.REVERSE?", a:"Reverses the motor's positive direction so both sides of a drivetrain move forward with the same positive power value.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is isBusy() used for?", a:"Checks if a motor is still moving toward its RUN_TO_POSITION target. Loop while isBusy() to wait for completion.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What does Thread.sleep() do?", a:"Pauses execution for N milliseconds. Avoid in active OpModes â€” use ElapsedTime for non-blocking timing instead.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the FTC config file?", a:"An XML file on the Robot Controller defining hardware device names and ports. Must match hardwareMap.get() names exactly.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is inheritance in Java?", a:"A class extends another to inherit its fields and methods. In FTC, your OpMode class extends LinearOpMode.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a null pointer exception?", a:"Calling a method on a null (uninitialized) object. Most common FTC bug â€” always initialize hardware before calling methods on it.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a for-each loop?", a:"for (DcMotor m : motors) { m.setPower(0); }. Iterates over any Iterable â€” cleaner than index-based loops.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"public vs. private vs. protected?", a:"Public: accessible everywhere. Private: only within the same class. Protected: within the class and its subclasses.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a constructor?", a:"A special method called when an object is created with 'new'. Same name as the class, no return type.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What are the DcMotor RunModes?", a:"RUN_WITHOUT_ENCODER, RUN_USING_ENCODER (velocity control), RUN_TO_POSITION, STOP_AND_RESET_ENCODER.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What is a PID controller?", a:"Proportional-Integral-Derivative: output = KpÃ—error + KiÃ—âˆ«error + KdÃ—(d error/dt). Drives a system toward a setpoint.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is RUN_TO_POSITION mode?", a:"A DcMotor RunMode using the built-in encoder and controller to autonomously drive to a target tick position.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a state machine in robotics?", a:"A design pattern where the robot is always in one defined state and transitions based on sensor input or elapsed time.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is Road Runner?", a:"An FTC motion planning library generating smooth trajectories and using odometry for accurate autonomous path following.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is encoder position measured in?", a:"Ticks â€” REV HD Hex Motor = 2240 ticks/rev, REV Core Hex = 288 ticks/rev. Use TICKS_PER_INCH constants to convert.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is mecanum drive math?", a:"Each wheel = axial Â± lateral Â± yaw. Front-left: +ax+lat+yaw, front-right: +ax-lat-yaw, back-left: +ax-lat+yaw, back-right: +ax+lat-yaw.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is EOCV?", a:"Easy OpenCV â€” FTC library enabling OpenCV camera processing on Android without a full TensorFlow pipeline.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an interface in Java?", a:"A contract defining method signatures a class must implement â€” e.g., a Subsystem interface with initialize() and update() methods.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What does ElapsedTime do?", a:"Tracks wall-clock time. .reset() starts it; .seconds()/.milliseconds() reads elapsed time. Great for autonomous timeouts.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is TFOD in FTC?", a:"TensorFlow Object Detection â€” uses a trained ML model on the camera to detect and classify game objects by type.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a try/catch in Java?", a:"Error handling: 'try' block runs; if an exception is thrown, the 'catch' block handles it without crashing the OpMode.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is polymorphism?", a:"A subclass used as its parent type. Lets you write general code (List<Subsystem>) that works on any implementing subclass.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a static variable or method?", a:"Belongs to the class, not an instance. Access via ClassName.field. Use for constants like TICKS_PER_INCH.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a HashMap in Java?", a:"Key-value data structure with O(1) lookup by key. HashMap<String, DcMotor> motors = new HashMap<>();", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Rev IMU in FTC?", a:"Built-in IMU on the REV Control Hub providing heading, pitch, and roll. Initialize with RevHubOrientationOnRobot.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an enum in Java?", a:"Fixed set of named constants: enum DriveMode { FIELD_CENTRIC, ROBOT_CENTRIC, SLOW_MODE }. Great for state machines.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is odometry in FTC?", a:"Using passive dead-wheel encoders (not connected to drive motors) to track the robot's X, Y, and heading position precisely.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is field-centric driving?", a:"Drive controls are relative to the field, not the robot. Input vectors are rotated by the gyro heading before applying to wheels.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is DcMotorEx?", a:"Extended FTC motor interface providing setVelocity() (ticks/sec), current sensing, and other advanced features beyond basic DcMotor.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"What is a volatile variable?", a:"Ensures reads/writes go to main memory rather than CPU cache â€” important for variables shared between multiple threads.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is the Builder pattern in Road Runner?", a:"trajectoryBuilder(startPose).forward(24).strafeRight(12).build(). Creates a reusable Trajectory or TrajectorySequence object.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a singleton in Java?", a:"A class with only one instance, accessed via a static method. Used in FTC for a shared hardware manager or telemetry wrapper.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is Java generics?", a:"Type parameters in angle brackets: List<DcMotor>. Provides compile-time type safety and avoids casting to the correct type.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a BulkRead in FTC?", a:"Reading all encoder/sensor data from a REV hub in a single I2C transaction instead of one per sensor â€” dramatically reduces loop time.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is an abstract class?", a:"Cannot be instantiated directly; may have abstract methods subclasses must implement. Like an interface but can hold state.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is setVelocity() in FTC?", a:"DcMotorEx method setting motor speed in ticks/second using closed-loop velocity control â€” more consistent than setPower().", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is an EOCV pipeline?", a:"Class extending OpenCvPipeline with processFrame(Mat) that processes each camera frame and returns a visualized output.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a command pattern in FTC?", a:"Wrapping actions in command objects that can be queued, cancelled, and sequenced â€” similar to WPILib Command-Based for FRC.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is Kotlin vs Java for FTC?", a:"Both are FTC SDK supported. Kotlin offers concise syntax, null safety, and extension functions â€” increasingly popular in competitive FTC.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a FTC OpMode control loop rate?", a:"Runs as fast as code allows, typically ~100Hz (10ms/loop) depending on sensor reads. BulkReads are key to keeping loop times low.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is PID tuning process?", a:"Start with Ki=Kd=0. Increase Kp until oscillation. Add Kd to damp. Add small Ki to remove steady-state error. Test iteratively.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a trajectory sequence in Road Runner?", a:"A sequence of trajectories, turns, and waits chained together with .addTemporalMarker() callbacks for mechanism actions mid-path.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is method overriding?", a:"Subclass provides its own implementation of a parent method. Annotate with @Override to catch typos at compile time.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW v6 ---
      { q:"What is a comment in Java?", a:"// single line or /* multi-line */. Comments are ignored by the compiler â€” use them to explain code.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a boolean in Java?", a:"A variable holding true or false. Used in if/while conditions: boolean isRunning = true;", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a String in Java?", a:"An immutable sequence of characters: String name = \"FTC Team\"; Supports .length(), .contains(), .substring(), .equals().", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is an array in Java?", a:"Fixed-size ordered collection: int[] speeds = new int[4]; Access by index: speeds[0]. Length via speeds.length.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the difference between int and double?", a:"int stores whole numbers (no decimal): int ticks = 2240. double stores floating-point: double power = 0.75. Use double for motor power values.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a while loop in Java?", a:"Repeats a block while a condition is true: while (opModeIsActive()) { driveRobot(); }. Ensure the condition can become false to avoid infinite loops.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is method overloading?", a:"Multiple methods with the same name but different parameters: drive(double power) and drive(double left, double right). Java picks the right one automatically.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a ternary operator?", a:"Shorthand if/else: double power = gamepad1.a ? 0.5 : 1.0. Reads as: if gamepad1.a is pressed, use 0.5, otherwise 1.0.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an ArrayList in Java?", a:"A resizable list: ArrayList<String> names = new ArrayList<>(); add(), remove(), get(i), size(). Backed by an array but auto-resizes.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Math class in Java?", a:"Math.abs(), Math.max(), Math.min(), Math.pow(), Math.sqrt(), Math.PI. Frequently used for motor power clamping and geometric calculations.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a switch statement?", a:"Multi-way branch: switch (state) { case INTAKE: ...; break; case SCORE: ...; break; default: ...; }. Cleaner than long if/else chains for states.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the @Override annotation?", a:"Tells the compiler a method intentionally overrides a parent class method. If no parent method matches, compilation fails â€” catches typos in method names.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is casting in Java?", a:"Converting between types: (int) 3.7 â†’ 3. (DcMotorEx) hardwareMap.get(DcMotor.class, \"arm\") casts a DcMotor to the extended DcMotorEx interface.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a functional interface in Java?", a:"An interface with exactly one abstract method â€” can be used as a lambda target. Runnable, Supplier<T>, Consumer<T> are common built-in functional interfaces.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is Java's Optional<T>?", a:"A container that may or may not hold a value â€” prevents null pointer exceptions. Optional.of(val), .empty(), .isPresent(), .orElse(default).", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is the synchronized keyword?", a:"Marks a method or block as thread-safe by acquiring the object's monitor lock. Use when multiple threads read/write shared robot state variables.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a weak reference in Java?", a:"A reference that doesn't prevent garbage collection. Used in caches where entries should be dropped when memory is low â€” rarely needed in FTC but important in larger apps.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is Java reflection?", a:"Inspecting or invoking classes/methods at runtime via Class.forName(), Method.invoke(). Used by the FTC SDK to discover and instantiate OpMode classes automatically.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a ConcurrentHashMap?", a:"A thread-safe HashMap from java.util.concurrent. Allows concurrent reads without locking and segments writes for better throughput than synchronized HashMap.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is tail recursion?", a:"Recursion where the recursive call is the last operation in the function. Some compilers optimize it to iteration. Java does NOT optimize tail recursion â€” watch for stack overflow.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

  // â”€â”€â”€ 2. ROBOT MECHANICS & DESIGN â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  mechanics: {
    name: "Robot Mechanics & Design",
    icon: "âš™ï¸",
    color: "#dc2626",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"What is a gear ratio?", a:"Input teeth Ã· output teeth. 20:60 = 3:1 reduction â€” output spins 3Ã— slower but produces 3Ã— more torque.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is tank drive?", a:"Two independently driven sides. Simple, robust, strong pushing power. Cannot strafe.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is mecanum drive?", a:"Four wheels with 45Â° rollers allow strafing and holonomic movement. Simpler than swerve, widely popular in FTC.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What does a linear slide do?", a:"Extends reach horizontally or vertically to grab, place, or hang. Often rack-and-pinion or string/pulley driven.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is COG (Center of Gravity)?", a:"Average position of weight distribution. Low COG = more stable under defense and acceleration.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a hex shaft?", a:"1/4\" hexagonal cross-section shaft that transfers torque without set screws â€” standard in the REV FTC ecosystem.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is compliance in an intake?", a:"Flexible design that deforms slightly when contacting game pieces, improving reliability and reducing jams.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a bearing?", a:"Reduces friction between rotating shaft and fixed structure, supports loads, extends component life.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is an omni wheel?", a:"Free-spinning rollers on the circumference allow sideways slip â€” reduces scrubbing when a tank drive turns.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a sprocket?", a:"Toothed wheel meshing with chain. Number of teeth determines chain drive ratio between two sprockets.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is an intake roller?", a:"Spinning tube or compliant wheels that grab and pull game pieces into the robot. Often runs on CRServos.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a hopper?", a:"Passive storage container collecting and holding game pieces after intake before scoring.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a COTS part?", a:"Commercial Off-The-Shelf â€” a pre-made part (REV kit, goBILDA channel) bought rather than custom-fabricated.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is polycarbonate (lexan)?", a:"Tough, transparent thermoplastic sheet used for robot side panels and protective covers â€” strong, light, easy to cut.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What is a worm gear?", a:"High-reduction, self-locking gear mesh. Holds position under gravity without power â€” good for arms, bad for back-drivability.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What does 'back-drivable' mean?", a:"A mechanism pushed back by external force. Spur gears back-drive freely; worm gears do not.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a four-bar linkage?", a:"4 rigid links (ground, crank, coupler, output) creating controlled arc motion. Used for arms and intakes.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a cantilever load?", a:"A load supported at only one end. Add a second support point to prevent shaft bending and bearing failures.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a cascade slide?", a:"Multi-stage slide extending sequentially â€” stage 2 extends only after stage 1 is fully out.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a continuous rigged slide?", a:"All stages extend simultaneously at the same speed for maximum range with uniform motion.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a pulley system?", a:"Rope over pulleys changes force direction or multiplies mechanical advantage â€” used in FTC climbers and slides.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a rack and pinion?", a:"Pinion gear meshes with linear rack to convert rotation to linear motion. Used in slides and steering.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is moment of inertia?", a:"Resistance to rotational acceleration. Mass near center = lower MOI = faster, more agile turns.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"Belt vs. chain drive?", a:"Belts: lighter, quieter, need tensioning. Chains: slip-proof, handle shock loads, noisier.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a dead axle?", a:"Non-rotating axle bearing weight while the wheel rotates around it on bearings â€” reduces motor shaft stress.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a spool in a winch?", a:"Cylinder around which string wraps as the motor rotates, converting rotation into linear cable travel.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a differential swerve?", a:"Swerve module using two co-axial motors â€” sum controls drive speed, difference controls steering angle.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a turret?", a:"Rotating platform letting a mechanism (shooter, arm) spin independently of the drivetrain heading.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a passive intake?", a:"Intake using the robot's forward motion and fixed geometry (wedges, ramps) to collect game pieces without active motors.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a clamping mechanism?", a:"Grips game pieces using opposing surfaces driven toward each other â€” often spring-loaded or motor-driven.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"What is swerve drive?", a:"Each wheel independently rotates and steers for full holonomic motion. Maximum maneuverability, very complex to build and code.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is structural rigidity?", a:"Resistance of the frame to bending and twisting under load. Rigid chassis improves drivetrain alignment and sensor accuracy.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a torsional load?", a:"Twisting force along a shaft's axis. Excess torsional load causes shaft failure â€” size shafts for expected torque.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a 2-speed transmission?", a:"Shifting gearbox with high gear (fast) and low gear (powerful) mode, switchable during a match via pneumatics or servo.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a bellcrank?", a:"L-shaped linkage converting direction of a pushing force by 90Â°. Used to actuate mechanisms in tight spaces.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a differential gearbox?", a:"Combines two motor inputs; sum drives output shaft, difference steers/rotates a second output.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a feeder system?", a:"Mechanism moving game pieces from intake storage to the scorer (shooter, placer) at a controlled rate.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Voronoi pattern in 3D printing?", a:"Complex lattice minimizing material while maintaining strength â€” used on FRC/FTC decorative panels and weight-reduction cutouts.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a snap ring (retaining ring)?", a:"Spring steel ring snapping into a shaft groove to prevent axial movement of gears or bearings.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is pitch chain vs. roller chain?", a:"Pitch = distance between link centers (#25, #35 etc.). FTC/FRC typically use #25/#35 roller chain. Larger pitch = higher load capacity.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW ---
      { q:"What is a rocker-bogie suspension?", a:"A passive suspension system allowing wheels to independently navigate uneven terrain â€” used in Mars rovers and some FRC robots for obstacle climbing.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a drivebase bumper rail?", a:"A horizontal structural member at the bottom of the chassis that the bumper mounts to. Must be within FIRST's specified height range from the ground.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a surgical tube in FTC?", a:"Elastic latex tubing used as a spring return or passive tensioning element in mechanisms. Cheap, lightweight, and easy to rig.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a tread-style drivetrain?", a:"Uses a continuous track (like a tank) instead of wheels. Excellent traction and obstacle crossing â€” rarely used in FTC/FRC due to weight and complexity.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a robot's footprint?", a:"The 2D area the robot occupies when viewed from above. Minimizing footprint helps with starting configuration and field navigation.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a pivot arm?", a:"An arm that rotates around a fixed pivot point. Simple, reliable, and easy to analyze â€” used for intakes, scoring mechanisms, and climbers.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a coaxial swerve module?", a:"A swerve module where the drive and steer mechanisms share the same central axis â€” compact but mechanically complex to design.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a parallel plate gripper?", a:"A gripper where two flat plates move toward each other to clamp a game piece â€” reliable and works on many object geometries.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is mechanical slop?", a:"Unwanted play or backlash in a mechanism caused by loose tolerances, worn gears, or poor assembly â€” degrades positioning accuracy.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a compliant wheel?", a:"A wheel made of soft material (foam, rubber) that deforms to grip irregular game pieces â€” common in FRC/FTC intake systems.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a tensegrity structure?", a:"A structure stabilized by continuous tension and discontinuous compression. Rarely used in FRC/FTC but studied for lightweight robot frames.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a variable-length linkage?", a:"A linkage where one or more links can change length during motion, often using a threaded rod or pneumatic cylinder as the variable link.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a capstan drive?", a:"String wraps multiple times around a smooth drum (capstan). Friction holds the string without it being tied â€” used in FTC string climbers.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a static vs. dynamic load?", a:"Static load: constant force (holding position). Dynamic load: time-varying force (motion, impacts). Design for peak dynamic loads, not just static.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is finite element analysis (FEA) for mechanisms?", a:"Simulates stress distribution in a part under load to identify high-stress regions. Used to validate CAD before machining or printing expensive parts.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a spatial mechanism?", a:"A mechanism with motion in 3D space rather than a single plane. Much harder to analyze â€” requires vector math or CAD simulation.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a detent mechanism?", a:"A spring-loaded ball or plunger that snaps into indexed positions on a shaft or plate â€” provides tactile stops without a locking mechanism.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is mechanical hysteresis?", a:"Lag between a mechanism's position and the input due to friction, elasticity, or backlash. Significant in high-precision positioning systems.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Peaucellier-Lipkin linkage?", a:"A linkage producing exact straight-line motion without a sliding joint. Historically significant; occasionally used in precision FRC mechanisms.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is topology optimization?", a:"A computational design method removing material from low-stress regions to minimize weight while maintaining structural strength â€” used with metal 3D printing.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

  // â”€â”€â”€ 3. ELECTRONICS & WIRING â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  electronics: {
    name: "Electronics & Wiring",
    icon: "âš¡",
    color: "#7c3aed",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"What is Ohm's Law?", a:"V = I Ã— R. Voltage = current Ã— resistance. Used to calculate wire gauge, fuse ratings, and voltage drops.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a motor controller?", a:"Converts a control signal (CAN, PWM) into variable voltage/current for a motor â€” SparkMAX, TalonFX, REV hub port.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a main breaker?", a:"Master ON/OFF switch and over-current protection for the entire robot electrical system.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"Wire gauge guide?", a:"6â€“8 AWG for battery/PDP mains; 10â€“12 AWG for high-current motors; 18â€“22 AWG for signal/sensor wires.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is an encoder?", a:"Sensor on a shaft outputting pulses as it rotates â€” measures position, velocity, and direction.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a limit switch?", a:"Mechanical switch triggered at a physical boundary â€” homes mechanisms, prevents over-travel, detects game pieces.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a REV Control Hub?", a:"FTC main controller â€” Android-based hub with 4 motor ports, 6 servo ports, digital/analog I/O, built-in IMU.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What does a fuse do?", a:"Melts and permanently breaks the circuit when current exceeds its rated value â€” protects wires from fire.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"Analog vs. digital sensors?", a:"Analog: variable voltage (0â€“3.3V) representing a range. Digital: binary HIGH/LOW â€” button pressed or not.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is wire management?", a:"Organizing and securing wires to prevent shorts, disconnections, and mechanism tangles. Leading cause of match failures if neglected.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a strain relief?", a:"Clamp securing wire near a connector preventing tension from pulling the connection loose during operation.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is continuity testing?", a:"Multimeter in continuity mode beeps when both wire ends are connected â€” verifies wiring is intact.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is wire tinning?", a:"Applying a small amount of solder to bare wire strands before inserting into a terminal â€” prevents fraying and improves contact.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a latching vs. momentary switch?", a:"Momentary: active only while pressed (spring returns). Latching: stays in position after press â€” used for power toggles.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What does a PDP/PDH do?", a:"Power Distribution Panel/Hub â€” distributes battery power to all subsystems with fused or breaker-protected outputs.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is CAN bus?", a:"Controller Area Network â€” serial protocol chaining SparkMAX, TalonSRX and other FRC devices. Two-wire differential signaling.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is PWM?", a:"Pulse Width Modulation â€” varying pulse duty cycle encodes speed or position. Used for servos and legacy motor controllers.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is voltage sag?", a:"Battery voltage drops under heavy load. FRC brownout triggers below ~6.8V, resetting the RoboRIO.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a gyroscope?", a:"Measures angular velocity and heading. Used for field-centric drive, auto-straight, and rotation PID loops.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a quadrature encoder?", a:"Two offset signals (A and B channels) together determine both speed and direction of shaft rotation.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is I2C?", a:"Inter-Integrated Circuit serial bus for FTC sensors (IMU, color, distance). Supports multiple devices per bus.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a REV Expansion Hub?", a:"Secondary FTC hub adding 4 motor ports, 6 servo ports, and I/O. Chains to Control Hub via RS485.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a BEC?", a:"Battery Eliminator Circuit â€” steps 12V battery voltage down to 5V/3.3V for servos and logic electronics.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a color sensor?", a:"Detects color or reflectance â€” identifies team elements, line following, or game piece presence in FTC.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"Series vs. parallel circuits?", a:"Series: same current, voltages add. Parallel: same voltage, currents add. Robot subsystems are wired in parallel to the battery.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a crimp connector?", a:"Wire connection where a metal sleeve is compressed around wire â€” more vibration-resistant than solder joints.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a voltage divider?", a:"Two resistors in series: midpoint voltage = Vin Ã— R2/(R1+R2). Scales sensor voltages to safe microcontroller input levels.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a capacitor used for?", a:"Stores and releases charge quickly â€” filters voltage noise, prevents brownouts, protects electronics from spikes.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a power budget?", a:"Spreadsheet estimating total current draw of all systems at peak load â€” ensures fuses/PDH channels are sized correctly.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a servo PWM range?", a:"Standard servos expect 50Hz PWM with 1ms pulse = 0Â° and 2ms pulse = 180Â°. FTC SDK abstracts this to 0.0â€“1.0.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"What is back-EMF?", a:"Voltage generated by a spinning motor acting against applied voltage. Motor controllers account for this effect.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a hall-effect sensor?", a:"Non-contact sensor detecting magnetic fields â€” used for absolute position sensing, RPM counting, and limit detection.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is signal noise?", a:"Unwanted interference corrupting sensor readings. Mitigated with shielded cables, digital filters, and good grounding.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is an absolute encoder?", a:"Reports actual shaft angular position (0â€“360Â°) even after power loss â€” unlike incremental encoders counting relative movement.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is thermal runaway in a motor?", a:"Overheating â†’ higher resistance â†’ more current â†’ more heat â€” destructive cycle leading to motor burnout if not interrupted.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a MOSFET?", a:"Transistor inside motor controllers switching high-current motor power using a low-current control signal.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a REV Power Distribution Hub?", a:"FRC PDH with 20 high-current channels, 4 low-current channels, CAN/USB monitoring, and integrated current sensing.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is isolation in robot wiring?", a:"Keeping signal/sensor wires physically separated from high-current motor wires to prevent EMI-induced noise.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"Why does current draw matter?", a:"Excessive draw trips breakers, heats wires, and browns out the battery â€” disabling the robot mid-match.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a through-hole vs. surface-mount component?", a:"Through-hole: leads go through PCB holes â€” easier to hand-solder. SMD: components sit on PCB surface â€” smaller, harder to solder by hand.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW ---
      { q:"What is a rocker switch?", a:"A switch that rocks between ON and OFF positions â€” used for panel-mounted power controls, often a main switch for non-primary power circuits.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a JST connector?", a:"A small, locking wire-to-wire or wire-to-board connector. Common in FTC for sensor and small motor connections due to its compact size.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a LED indicator on a robot?", a:"An LED wired to a digital output provides visual feedback about robot state (enabled/disabled, intake active) without opening a dashboard.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a servo extension cable?", a:"A pre-made cable with servo-style connectors (signal/power/ground) used to extend the reach of a servo wire to a distant mounting location.\", label:\"beginner", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a multimeter?", a:"A test instrument measuring voltage, current, resistance, and continuity. Essential for diagnosing wiring faults and verifying circuit health.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a power pole connector (Anderson)?", a:"A genderless, modular connector rated for high current. Standard on FRC main power runs â€” cannot be plugged in backwards.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a twisted pair cable?", a:"Two wires twisted together to cancel electromagnetic interference. CAN bus and encoder cables are often twisted pairs for noise rejection.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a pulse counter?", a:"A digital input mode counting rising or falling edges on a signal â€” used to count encoder pulses or measure sensor trigger frequency.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an optocoupler?", a:"An electrical component isolating two circuits using light â€” input LED shines on a phototransistor. Protects sensitive electronics from high-voltage transients.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a PWM frequency?", a:"How many pulses per second the PWM signal sends. Standard servos use 50Hz; motor controllers typically use 20kHz+ for smooth motor control.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a zero-crossing circuit?", a:"Detects when an AC signal crosses zero volts â€” used in motor speed controllers for precise commutation timing in brushless motor drivers.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is impedance?", a:"The AC equivalent of resistance, combining resistance and reactance (from capacitors and inductors). Important when designing circuits with AC signals or high-frequency PWM.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a relay?", a:"An electromechanical switch controlled by a small current that switches a much larger current. Used in FRC for pneumatic solenoids and some custom circuits.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a motor's back-EMF constant (kV)?", a:"Voltage generated per unit of angular velocity: kV = V/Ï‰. A higher kV motor spins faster at 12V but produces less torque at stall.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a H-bridge?", a:"A circuit with four switches arranged in an H pattern allowing current to flow through a motor in either direction â€” the core of every brushed motor controller.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a bootstrap circuit in a motor controller?", a:"A technique to drive the high-side MOSFET gate above the supply voltage by temporarily charging a capacitor â€” essential in H-bridge motor controller design.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is dead-time in a motor controller?", a:"A brief delay inserted between switching the high and low side MOSFETs to prevent both from conducting simultaneously (shoot-through), which would short the supply.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is field-oriented control (FOC)?", a:"A brushless motor control technique aligning current with the rotor's magnetic field for maximum torque efficiency â€” more efficient than simple 6-step commutation.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a current sense resistor?", a:"A very low-value resistor in series with a motor. Measuring the voltage drop across it (V=IR) gives the motor current â€” used for current limiting and fault detection.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is slew rate limiting?", a:"Artificially limiting how fast a motor controller changes output to reduce current spikes and mechanical stress during rapid direction changes.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

  // â”€â”€â”€ 4. GAME STRATEGY & SCOUTING â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  strategy: {
    name: "Game Strategy & Scouting",
    icon: "ðŸŽ¯",
    color: "#1d4ed8",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"What is scouting in FIRST?", a:"Collecting performance data on teams during matches to inform alliance selection and match strategy decisions.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a cycler robot?", a:"Quickly and reliably picks up and scores game pieces repeatedly in teleop for maximum point output.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is end game?", a:"Last 20â€“30 seconds of a match â€” often worth extra points (climbing, parking). Heavily influences robot design.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is gracious professionalism?", a:"FIRST core value: compete hard, respect all teams. Win and lose with grace. Help others succeed.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is auto consistency?", a:"Reliably completing the same autonomous routine every match. Consistent simple beats unreliable complex.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is cycle time?", a:"Time for one full pick-up-and-score cycle. Shorter = more game pieces scored per match.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a scouting app?", a:"Mobile/web app recording team performance per match, aggregating stats, and generating picklist reports.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What does 'leaving on the field' mean?", a:"A robot disabled/broken mid-match â€” major reliability red flag in alliance selection decision-making.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is pit scouting?", a:"Visiting a team's pit to learn about capabilities, auto routines, and reliability before seeing them in matches.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a picklist?", a:"Ranked list of teams your alliance wants to pick â€” prepared before alliance selection begins at each event.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What is OPR?", a:"Offensive Power Rating â€” estimates points contributed to alliance per match, solved via linear algebra from match scores.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is DPR?", a:"Defensive Power Rating â€” estimates how many points a team takes away from opposing alliances per match.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is CCWM?", a:"Calculated Contribution to Winning Margin = OPR âˆ’ DPR. Positive = net positive alliance contribution.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What are Ranking Points (RP)?", a:"Bonus points per qualification match for objectives (win + game-specific milestones). Determines seeding.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is alliance selection?", a:"Top-8 seeds each pick 2 alliance partners. Complementary robots maximize alliance scoring potential.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a tiebreaker?", a:"When RP is tied, tiebreakers applied in order: average match score, then auto score, then game-specific metrics.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a super scout?", a:"Watches the whole field tracking defense, fouls, and strategy patterns invisible from single-team match data.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"Quals vs. elims?", a:"Quals determine seeding via RP. Elims are bracket-style best-of-3 by pre-selected alliances for the event title.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is The Blue Alliance (TBA)?", a:"Community database of FRC match results, team history, OPR calculations, and event data accessible via free API.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is banking autonomous?", a:"Choosing a simple, reliable auto to guarantee points rather than risking a complex routine that might fail.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"Key scouting metrics?", a:"Auto points, teleop cycles, end-game success, defense effectiveness, and reliability (matches with no failures).", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a district system?", a:"Teams earn points across multiple small events to qualify for District Championship â€” alternative to single regional events.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is scouting redundancy?", a:"Multiple scouts independently tracking the same team, then cross-validating data to catch errors and outliers.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"What is EPA?", a:"Expected Points Added â€” Statbotics metric measuring how much a team raises alliance expected score above baseline. More accurate than OPR.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is match prediction?", a:"Using OPRs and robot capability data to estimate expected match scores and plan upcoming match strategy.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is data normalization in scouting?", a:"Adjusting raw scores to account for alliance partner/opponent strength â€” gives fairer individual team ratings.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is defense in FRC/FTC?", a:"Legally blocking, pushing, or disrupting opponents to reduce their cycle rate. Alliance captain decides when to play.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is first-pick vs. second-pick strategy?", a:"First pick: highest-OPR available. Second pick: fills gaps â€” defense, reliable auto, or consistent end-game.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is sandbagging?", a:"Intentionally performing below capability to lower seeding. Poor sportsmanship in the FIRST community.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a 'cannot be defended' robot?", a:"A robot so fast/well-designed that assigning a defender costs the opponent more than leaving it free.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a penalty strategy?", a:"Designing play to legally bait opponents into committing penalties â€” controversial but present in high-level play.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a team's 'floor' vs. 'ceiling'?", a:"Floor = minimum reliable performance. Ceiling = theoretical maximum. Alliance selection favors high floors over high ceilings.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is scouting bias?", a:"Tendency to over-rate familiar teams or under-rate unfamiliar ones. Mitigated with standardized forms and multiple scouts.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW ---
      { q:"What is a match schedule?", a:"The pre-published list of which teams play against each other in each qualification match. Released at the start of each event.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a head referee?", a:"The official overseeing match play, making final ruling calls on penalties and game piece legality at each competition event.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a human player in FRC/FTC?", a:"A team member positioned at a specific field location who can interact with game pieces (feed balls, collect from loading stations) during matches.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a robot inspector?", a:"A FIRST volunteer who verifies each robot meets game manual rules (size, weight, materials) before the team is allowed to compete.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a technical foul?", a:"A more serious rule violation incurring a larger point penalty than a standard foul â€” often for repeated or egregious infractions.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is field reset?", a:"The process between matches where volunteers reset game pieces, field elements, and zone markings to their starting positions.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a match replay?", a:"A rare FIRST ruling granting a rematch if a field fault (FMS error, field element failure) materially affected match outcome.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is robot targeting priority?", a:"Deciding which game elements to score, in what order, during teleop â€” based on point value, robot capability, and field position.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a defensive 'box'?", a:"Keeping your defensive robot between the opponent and their scoring zone at all times, forcing detours that cost cycle time.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a 'parking' bonus?", a:"End-game points earned for moving your robot to a specific field zone. Often guaranteed â€” every robot should be capable of parking.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a co-opertition bonus?", a:"Some FIRST games award bonus ranking points for both alliances cooperatively completing a shared objective, rewarding collaborative play.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an auto path conflict?", a:"When two robots on the same alliance plan autonomous paths that cross â€” alliances must coordinate to avoid collisions during autonomous.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a 'safe' autonomous?", a:"An auto routine that reliably scores points without risking penalty or leaving the robot in a bad position for teleop.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is match film analysis?", a:"Reviewing video recordings of matches to evaluate robot performance, driver decisions, and opponent tendencies for strategic adjustment.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is expected value in strategy decisions?", a:"Probability Ã— outcome value. E.g., a risky auto with 60% success rate scores 10pts â†’ EV=6. A safe auto scoring 5pts every time has EV=5 â†’ risky is better here.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is alliance color assignment?", a:"At each event teams are assigned Red or Blue alliance for each match. Strategy and auto paths are often color-dependent.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a strategy 'script'?", a:"A pre-planned sequence of actions for each phase (auto, early teleop, end game) that the drive team executes with minimal improvisation.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is throughput optimization?", a:"Maximizing game pieces scored per match by minimizing dead time â€” travel time, wait time at loading station, and missed pickups.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a scouting 'consensus meeting'?", a:"A structured session where all scouts share observations and reach agreement on team ratings before finalizing the picklist.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a 'defense tax'?", a:"The estimated reduction in your own offense output when running a robot as a defender â€” factored into alliance strategy decisions.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

      // BEGINNER

      { q:"What is a for loop in Python?", a:"Iterates over any sequence: for x in [1, 2, 3]: print(x). Use range(n) to loop n times: for i in range(5).", level:"beginner" },

      { q:"What is a while loop?", a:"Repeats while a condition is True: while count < 10: count += 1. Always ensure the condition eventually becomes False.", level:"beginner" },

      { q:"What is a Python dictionary?", a:"Unordered key-value mapping: {'key': value}. Access with d['key'] or d.get('key', default).", level:"intermediate" },

      { q:"What is a try/except block?", a:"Error handling: 'try' block runs; 'except' catches exceptions instead of crashing the program.", level:"intermediate" },

      { q:"What is a virtual environment?", a:"Isolated Python environment (venv) keeping project dependencies separate from system Python.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is *args and **kwargs?", a:"*args: extra positional args as tuple. **kwargs: extra keyword args as dict. Used for flexible function signatures.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Python set?", a:"Unordered unique elements: {1, 2, 3}. Fast membership testing, supports union/intersection/difference.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What does json.dumps() do?", a:"Converts Python object to JSON string. json.loads() parses JSON text back to Python dict/list.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is requests.get()?", a:"Fetches data from a URL (e.g., TBA API). Returns Response â€” use .json() to parse the body.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an f-string?", a:"Python 3.6+ string interpolation: f'Team {num} scored {score:.1f}'. Embeds variables inline.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is DataFrame.merge()?", a:"Joins two DataFrames on a common column like SQL JOIN: df.merge(other, on='team', how='left').", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is sorting with a key?", a:"sorted(teams, key=lambda t: t['opr'], reverse=True). The key function extracts the comparison value.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"How is OPR calculated in Python?", a:"np.linalg.lstsq(alliance_matrix, scores). Rows = matches, columns = teams (1 if on alliance, 0 if not).", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What does async/await do?", a:"Enables non-blocking code. 'await' pauses during I/O, letting other coroutines run concurrently.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a generator?", a:"Function using 'yield' returning values one at a time. Memory-efficient for large datasets.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a dataclass?", a:"@dataclass decorator auto-generates __init__, __repr__, __eq__ from annotated fields â€” less boilerplate.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is Plotly?", a:"Interactive charting library. Charts users can zoom, hover, filter â€” better than matplotlib for web dashboards.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is the walrus operator (:=)?", a:"Python 3.8+ assignment expression: while chunk := f.read(8192): process(chunk). Assigns and tests at once.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is type hinting?", a:"def score(team: str, pts: int) -> float. Annotates types for readability and IDE checking â€” not enforced at runtime.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is SQLite in Python?", a:"Built-in lightweight SQL database (import sqlite3). Stores scouting data locally without a full database server.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Python abstract base class?", a:"from abc import ABC, abstractmethod â€” defines methods subclasses must implement. Enforces interface contracts at class definition.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is multiprocessing vs. threading?", a:"Threading: concurrent but limited by the GIL. Multiprocessing: separate processes bypassing the GIL â€” true parallelism for CPU tasks.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is pandas apply()?", a:"Applies a custom function to each row or column: df['result'] = df.apply(lambda row: compute(row), axis=1).", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Python namedtuple?", a:"collections.namedtuple('Point', ['x', 'y']) creates a tuple subclass with named fields: p.x, p.y. Immutable and memory-efficient.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is pandas pivot_table()?", a:"Creates a spreadsheet-style pivot table from DataFrame data â€” great for summarizing scouting stats by team and metric.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW ---
      { q:"What is a Python comment?", a:"Text after # that Python ignores: # This is a comment. Used to explain code. Multi-line comments use triple quotes: '''like this'''.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is None in Python?", a:"Python's null value representing the absence of a value. Always check with 'x is None', not 'x == None'.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a boolean in Python?", a:"A True or False value. Used in if statements and while loops. Boolean operators: and, or, not.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is range() in Python?", a:"Generates a sequence of numbers: range(5) â†’ 0,1,2,3,4. range(2,8) â†’ 2â€“7. range(0,10,2) â†’ 0,2,4,6,8.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a Python import statement?", a:"Loads a module: import math, import pandas as pd, from datetime import datetime. Makes external code available in your script.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is string slicing?", a:"Extracting part of a string: s[0:3] gets characters 0,1,2. s[-3:] gets last 3. s[::2] gets every other character.", level:"beginner" },
