      { q:"What does .strip() do in Python?", a:"Removes leading and trailing whitespace (spaces, newlines, tabs) from a string: '  hello  '.strip() â†’ 'hello'.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is list .append() vs .extend()?", a:".append(x) adds one item to the end. .extend([x,y]) adds all items from another iterable. [1,2].extend([3,4]) â†’ [1,2,3,4].", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a Python dictionary .items()?", a:"Returns key-value pairs as tuples: for key, val in d.items():. Lets you iterate over both keys and values simultaneously.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Python Counter?", a:"collections.Counter({'a':3, 'b':1}) counts occurrences in an iterable. Counter('banana') â†’ {'a':3,'n':2,'b':1}. Has .most_common() method.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is pandas .value_counts()?", a:"Returns a Series with counts of unique values in a column: df['team'].value_counts(). Useful for scouting data frequency analysis.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Python os.path module?", a:"Provides file path utilities: os.path.join(), os.path.exists(), os.path.dirname(). Essential for portable file handling across operating systems.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is exception chaining in Python?", a:"raise ValueError('msg') from original_error â€” preserves the original exception context when re-raising. Helps with debugging complex error chains.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Python property setter?", a:"@name.setter decorator lets you run code when a property is assigned: obj.speed = 5 can validate the value before storing it.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Python __str__ vs __repr__?", a:"__str__: human-readable string for print(). __repr__: unambiguous developer string for debugging. If only one is defined, __repr__ serves both.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is functools.lru_cache?", a:"@lru_cache(maxsize=128) memoizes a function's results â€” caches outputs for repeated inputs. Speeds up expensive calculations called with the same arguments.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Python descriptor?", a:"An object implementing __get__, __set__, or __delete__ that customizes attribute access on a class. The mechanism behind @property and many frameworks.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is asyncio.gather()?", a:"Runs multiple coroutines concurrently and waits for all: results = await asyncio.gather(fetch(url1), fetch(url2)). Much faster than sequential awaits.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is Python's GIL?", a:"Global Interpreter Lock â€” prevents multiple threads from executing Python bytecode simultaneously. Threading is limited to I/O concurrency; use multiprocessing for CPU parallelism.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Python metaclass?", a:"A class whose instances are classes. class Meta(type): ... controls class creation. Used in ORMs, ABCs, and framework magic â€” rarely needed in robot code.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

  // â”€â”€â”€ 6. CAD & DESIGN â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  cad: {
    name: "CAD & Design",
    icon: "ðŸ“",
    color: "#0891b2",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"What is CAD?", a:"Computer-Aided Design â€” software for creating precise 2D drawings and 3D models before physical fabrication.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is Onshape?", a:"Cloud-based CAD tool popular in FTC/FRC. Files stored online â€” real-time multi-user collaboration on the same model.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a sketch in CAD?", a:"2D profile of constrained geometry (lines, arcs, circles) on a plane â€” foundation for 3D features.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is an extrude?", a:"Pulls a 2D sketch into a 3D solid by a specified distance. The most fundamental 3D modeling operation.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a fillet?", a:"Rounds a sharp edge with a specified radius. Reduces stress concentrations on printed or machined parts.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a chamfer?", a:"Flat angled cut at an edge. Eases assembly (e.g., chamfering a bearing pocket) and removes sharp corners.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is FDM 3D printing?", a:"Fused Deposition Modeling â€” melts filament (PLA, PETG, ABS) layer by layer. Most common method on FIRST teams.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is infill in 3D printing?", a:"Internal structure density (0â€“100%). Higher = stronger and heavier. 20â€“40% typical for functional robot parts.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is laser cutting?", a:"Cutting flat profiles from polycarbonate, aluminum, or wood with high precision â€” fast for plates, brackets, panels.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"Part vs. assembly?", a:"A part is a single solid body. An assembly combines multiple parts with mates to model how they fit and move together.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a BOM?", a:"Bill of Materials â€” list of all parts and quantities in an assembly, auto-generated from the CAD model.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is goBILDA?", a:"Popular FTC COTS hardware system offering aluminum channel, shafts, hubs, and brackets designed for easy assembly.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What is a revolve?", a:"Rotates a 2D profile around an axis to create a rotationally symmetric 3D body â€” shafts, wheels, hubs.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a mate in assembly?", a:"Relationship between two parts defining relative position and motion â€” coincident, concentric, revolute, etc.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a design constraint?", a:"Rule locking sketch geometry (parallel, equal, fixed distance). Fully constrained sketches turn black in most CAD tools.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is tolerance?", a:"Acceptable dimensional variation range (e.g., 25mm Â± 0.1mm). Critical for mating parts like shafts in bearings.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a parametric model?", a:"Model driven by named dimensions â€” changing one parameter updates all related geometry automatically.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is sheet metal design?", a:"Modeling thin parts with bends. Software calculates bend allowance so flat pattern is accurate for laser cutting.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a hole tool?", a:"Creates standard-sized holes (clearance, tap, counterbore) with correct dimensions for specific bolt sizes.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a STEP file?", a:"Universal CAD exchange format (.step/.stp) sharing 3D models between different CAD programs without geometry loss.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is DFM?", a:"Design for Manufacturability â€” designing parts that are easy and cheap to make, minimizing complex features and tight tolerances.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a mirror/pattern feature?", a:"Duplicates geometry symmetrically (mirror) or in linear/circular arrays (pattern). Saves time on symmetric designs.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a sub-assembly?", a:"Assembly nested inside a larger one â€” organizes complex robots into reusable groups (gearbox, intake, climber).", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"PETG vs. PLA?", a:"PLA: easy to print, less durable, lower heat tolerance. PETG: tougher, impact-resistant, better heat tolerance. Better for robot parts.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is print orientation?", a:"Layer height determines resolution and speed. Parts are weaker along Z-axis (between layers) than X/Y â€” orient accordingly.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a technical drawing?", a:"2D document showing a part with dimensions, tolerances, and notes for manufacturing machined or outsourced parts.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a design iteration?", a:"Building and testing a prototype, identifying failures, then redesigning. Most successful mechanisms go through 3+ iterations.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a robot layout sketch?", a:"Top-level 2D sketch in CAD defining overall robot dimensions, bumper constraints, and subsystem placement before detailed modeling.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"What is FEA?", a:"Finite Element Analysis â€” simulates stress, deflection, or heat under loads by dividing the model into tiny elements.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is version control in Onshape?", a:"Auto-saves all changes. Create versions/tags to mark milestones; branch and merge designs like Git for code.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is design intent?", a:"The reasoning behind dimension and constraint choices. A well-designed model updates predictably when key dimensions change.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a loft feature?", a:"Creates a 3D solid by blending smoothly between two or more 2D profiles on different planes.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a sweep feature?", a:"Extrudes a 2D profile along a 3D path curve â€” used for tubing, handles, and wire channels.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is SolidWorks?", a:"Professional parametric CAD common in FRC. Powerful simulation and large part library support. Desktop installation required.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a keyed shaft?", a:"Shaft with a flat keyway groove. A matching metal key locks a gear/sprocket to the shaft, preventing slipping.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is an assembly interference check?", a:"CAD tool detecting when two parts occupy the same space â€” finds design collisions before physical fabrication.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is photogrammetry in robotics?", a:"Using multiple camera photos of a physical object to generate a 3D CAD model â€” useful for modeling irregular game pieces.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a fastener library in CAD?", a:"Built-in or downloadable collection of standard hardware models (bolts, nuts, shafts) for inserting into assemblies.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW ---
      { q:"What is a 3D printer slicer?", a:"Software converting a 3D model into layer-by-layer print instructions (G-code): Cura, PrusaSlicer, Bambu Studio. Controls layer height, infill, speed, and supports.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a print bed?", a:"The flat surface a 3D print is built on. Must be level and at the correct temperature (60Â°C for PLA, 80Â°C for PETG) for good first-layer adhesion.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a hex bore?", a:"A hexagonal hole in a gear, wheel, or hub sized to fit a hex shaft â€” transfers torque without set screws. Standard in REV and goBILDA systems.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a counterbore vs countersink?", a:"Counterbore: flat-bottomed cylindrical recess for socket head screws. Countersink: conical recess for flat-head screws. Both allow fasteners to sit flush.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a clearance hole vs tap hole?", a:"Clearance hole: large enough for a bolt to pass through freely. Tap hole: smaller, threads are cut into it to accept a bolt directly without a nut.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is 'press fit' tolerance?", a:"An interference fit where the hole is slightly smaller than the shaft â€” parts are forced together and held by friction. Used for bearings in bearing pockets.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a running clearance?", a:"A small gap (0.1â€“0.3mm) between a rotating part and its housing, allowing free rotation without binding. Designed into all rotating shaft and sleeve fits.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a spline shaft?", a:"A shaft with multiple equally-spaced keyway grooves around its circumference. Allows more torque transfer than a single key and can slide axially while transmitting torque.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a surface finish in manufacturing?", a:"The texture of a machined surface, measured in Ra (average roughness). Finer finish = lower friction and better sealing but costs more to machine.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is GD&T (Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing)?", a:"A symbolic language on engineering drawings specifying allowable variations in form, orientation, and position â€” more precise than Â± tolerances alone.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a reference dimension?", a:"A dimension shown in parentheses on a drawing that is not controlled â€” provided for information only (e.g., overall assembly length derived from other dims).", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is anodizing?", a:"An electrochemical process creating a hard, corrosion-resistant oxide layer on aluminum parts. Can be colored. Common for decorative and protective robot panels.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a living hinge?", a:"A thin, flexible section of plastic connecting two rigid parts, flexing repeatedly without breaking. Used in FTC intake flaps and game piece deflectors.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a design checklist before printing?", a:"Verify: wall thickness â‰¥1.2mm, no unsupported overhangs >45Â°, correct tolerances on mating features, correct filament material, and correct scale/units.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is CNC milling?", a:"Computer-controlled cutting machine removing material from a block (usually aluminum) using rotating end mills. Produces precise custom metal parts for robot frames.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is CAM (Computer-Aided Manufacturing)?", a:"Software generating CNC machine toolpaths from a CAD model. Fusion 360's CAM workspace converts 3D geometry into G-code instructions for mills and lathes.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a design for assembly (DFA) principle?", a:"Design parts that can be assembled quickly with minimal tools, few fasteners, and obvious orientation â€” reduces build time and assembly errors.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a weldment analysis in CAD?", a:"Simulating the behavior of a welded frame structure under load. Checks if welds and members are strong enough for the robot's operating conditions.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is generative design?", a:"An AI-driven CAD feature that automatically generates optimized part geometries given constraints (loads, mounting points, materials) â€” used for lightweight FRC brackets.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a model-based definition (MBD)?", a:"Embedding all manufacturing information (tolerances, surface finish, material) directly in the 3D CAD model rather than on a 2D drawing â€” modern manufacturing standard.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

  // â”€â”€â”€ 7. GIT & VERSION CONTROL â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  git: {
    name: "Git & Version Control",
    icon: "ðŸŒ¿",
    color: "#166534",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"What is Git?", a:"Distributed version control system tracking file changes over time. Enables collaboration, branching, and rollback.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is git init?", a:"Initializes a new Git repo in the current directory, creating a hidden .git folder.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is git clone?", a:"Downloads a remote repository to your local machine, including all history and branches.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a commit?", a:"Permanent snapshot of staged changes in Git history. Unique hash, author, timestamp, and message.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is git status?", a:"Shows modified, staged, and untracked files â€” first command for checking your working directory state.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is git add?", a:"Stages changes for the next commit: git add filename or git add . to stage everything. Required before git commit.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is git commit?", a:"Saves staged changes permanently: git commit -m 'Your message here'. Always write a descriptive message.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is git push?", a:"Uploads local commits to a remote repository (e.g., GitHub), making them visible to teammates.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is git pull?", a:"Fetches remote changes and merges them into your current local branch.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a GitHub repository?", a:"A cloud-hosted Git repository on github.com. Enables sharing code, collaboration, issue tracking, and pull requests.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a branch?", a:"Lightweight pointer to a commit. Branches isolate feature development from the main codebase.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is .gitignore?", a:"File listing patterns Git should not track â€” build outputs, .DS_Store, API keys. Keeps repos clean.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What is the staging area?", a:"Preparation zone where you select changes with git add before committing them.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is git log?", a:"Displays commit history: hashes, authors, dates, and messages in reverse chronological order.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is git diff?", a:"Shows line-by-line differences between working directory and last commit, or between any two commits/branches.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a merge conflict?", a:"Two branches edit the same line differently. Git marks the conflict; you manually resolve it.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is git merge?", a:"Combines changes from one branch into another. Same-line edits create merge conflicts to resolve manually.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a pull request (PR)?", a:"GitHub feature requesting branch merge into another. Enables code review and discussion before merging.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is git stash?", a:"Temporarily saves uncommitted changes to a stack so you can switch branches. Restore with git stash pop.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is git fetch?", a:"Downloads remote changes without merging â€” lets you inspect what changed before running git merge.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a fork on GitHub?", a:"Personal copy of someone else's repo on your GitHub account. Standard workflow for open-source FTC library contributions.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a tag in Git?", a:"Named pointer to a specific commit marking release versions (v1.0, competition-day-2025). Tags don't move.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is HEAD in Git?", a:"Pointer to the current commit/branch you're on. 'Detached HEAD' = checked out a commit directly, not a branch.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a code review?", a:"Teammate examines your PR for bugs, style, and correctness before merging. Essential for maintaining code quality.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What makes a good commit message?", a:"Specific and concise: 'Fix mecanum strafe drift in teleop'. Present tense. Reference issue numbers if applicable.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"What is git rebase?", a:"Replays commits from one branch onto another â€” linear history, cleaner than merge, but rewrites hashes.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is git reset?", a:"Moves branch pointer to earlier commit. --soft keeps staged changes; --hard discards all uncommitted changes.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is git cherry-pick?", a:"Applies one specific commit from another branch onto the current branch without merging entire branch history.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is git bisect?", a:"Binary search tool finding which commit introduced a bug by checking midpoints and marking them good/bad.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is git blame?", a:"Shows which commit and author last modified each line of a file â€” useful for understanding why code was written a certain way.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a branch protection rule?", a:"GitHub setting requiring PR reviews or passing CI checks before code can be merged into a protected branch.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a GitHub Action?", a:"Automated CI/CD workflow triggered by Git events. Used to run tests, lint code, or auto-deploy documentation.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is interactive rebase?", a:"git rebase -i lets you edit, squash, reorder, or drop commits before pushing â€” useful for cleaning up messy history.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a squash commit?", a:"Combines multiple commits into one. Often done before merging a PR to keep the main branch history clean.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is git reflog?", a:"Local log of all HEAD movements including resets and rebases â€” lets you recover from accidental git reset --hard.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a commit hook?", a:"Scripts in .git/hooks running automatically on Git events (pre-commit). Used to run linters or tests before committing.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Git submodule?", a:"Pointer to a specific commit of another Git repo embedded inside yours â€” keeps dependencies at a pinned version.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW v6 ---
      { q:"What is version control and why use it?", a:"A system tracking all changes to files over time, letting you revert mistakes and collaborate without overwriting each other's work.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a repository host?", a:"A service storing Git repositories online: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket. GitHub is most popular for FIRST teams â€” free for public and educational repos.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is git checkout?", a:"Switches to a different branch or restores a file: git checkout main, git checkout feature-branch, git checkout -- file.java to discard changes.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a remote URL?", a:"The address of a hosted repository: https://github.com/org/repo.git or git@github.com:org/repo.git (SSH). Set with git remote add origin <url>.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is git switch?", a:"Modern replacement for git checkout (for branch switching): git switch main, git switch -c new-branch. Avoids ambiguity with the old checkout command.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a README.md?", a:"A Markdown file in the root of a repo describing the project â€” what it does, how to set it up, team info. Rendered automatically on GitHub.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a GitHub issue?", a:"A tracked task, bug report, or feature request in a repository. Can be referenced in commits (#42) and closed automatically when a PR merges.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a GitHub milestone?", a:"A collection of issues grouped by goal or deadline (e.g., 'Week 3 Build Sprint'). Tracks progress toward a specific objective.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is git shortlog?", a:"git shortlog -sn shows commit counts per author. Useful for understanding team contribution distribution without reading full git log output.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a GitHub project board?", a:"A Kanban-style board linked to issues and PRs in a repo. Teams use it to visualize tasks in To Do / In Progress / Done columns.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is git clean?", a:"Removes untracked files from the working directory: git clean -fd removes untracked files and directories. Irreversible â€” use with care.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a merge commit?", a:"A special commit created when branches are merged, having two parent commits. git merge --no-ff always creates one even for fast-forward merges.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a detached HEAD state?", a:"Occurs when you check out a commit directly (not a branch). New commits won't belong to any branch â€” create a new branch first if you want to keep them.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is git archive?", a:"Creates a zip/tar of a repo at a specific commit without .git history: git archive --format=zip HEAD > release.zip. Good for sharing code snapshots.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Git LFS?", a:"Large File Storage â€” extension storing large binary files (CAD, images, compiled binaries) outside the main repo, replacing them with pointers. Keeps repo size manageable.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a signed commit?", a:"A commit cryptographically signed with a GPG key, verifying the author's identity. GitHub shows a 'Verified' badge â€” important for supply chain security.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Git worktree?", a:"git worktree add allows checking out a second branch into a separate directory simultaneously â€” useful for comparing two versions without stashing.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is trunk-based development?", a:"A branching strategy where all developers commit directly to main (trunk) with very short-lived feature branches. Requires robust CI and feature flags.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a git patch?", a:"git format-patch generates email-style patch files from commits. git am applies them. Used to share changes without a shared remote â€” common in open-source.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is git notes?", a:"Allows attaching arbitrary text to commits without modifying them: git notes add -m 'Tested at comp' HEAD. Notes are stored separately from the commit object.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

  // â”€â”€â”€ 8. OUTREACH & COMMUNITY â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  outreach: {
    name: "Outreach & Community",
    icon: "ðŸŒ",
    color: "#be185d",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"What is outreach in FIRST?", a:"Activities engaging the community: teaching STEM, mentoring teams, hosting events, or partnering with sponsors.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is STEM?", a:"Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics â€” the fields FIRST aims to inspire students to pursue through robotics.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a STEM demo event?", a:"Public demonstration of your robot at schools, fairs, or community events to inspire interest in STEM.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is gracious professionalism in outreach?", a:"Treating partner organizations, sponsors, and community members with the same respect shown on the competition field.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a FIRST alumni?", a:"A former FIRST participant. Alumni serve as mentors, judges, volunteers, and sponsors â€” a lifelong resource.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is volunteerism in FIRST?", a:"Members serving as referees, field reset crew, or judges at events. Fulfills FIRST values and earns outreach recognition.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a community partner?", a:"Local organization (library, school, civic group) collaborating with the team to deliver regular outreach programs.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is social media's role?", a:"Shares progress and impact online, builds team brand, attracts sponsors, and inspires others to join FIRST.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is 'paying it forward'?", a:"Helping other teams succeed â€” sharing designs, code, or knowledge even with competitors. Core to FIRST culture.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What is the Impact Award?", a:"FIRST's highest honor â€” given to the team best demonstrating FIRST's mission and the most significant sustained community impact.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Engineering Inspiration Award?", a:"Recognizes a team excelling at spreading FIRST values and STEM enthusiasm into their school and community.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is rookie team mentorship?", a:"Experienced teams helping new FIRST teams learn robot building, programming, and competition culture.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What should an outreach log track?", a:"Date, event name, hours, people reached, members involved, and a brief description of measured impact.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a sponsor pitch?", a:"Presentation to a potential business sponsor explaining your mission, funding needs, and community benefit.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What makes strong outreach documentation?", a:"Specific numbers (students reached, hours, schools), photos, testimonials, and measurable outcomes.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a 501(c)(3) status?", a:"Non-profit tax-exempt status allowing the team to accept tax-deductible donations â€” makes sponsoring more attractive.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a grant in FIRST?", a:"Funding awarded by a foundation, company, or FIRST itself to teams demonstrating need, strong outreach, or specific goals.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Dean's List nomination?", a:"Award for exceptional student leaders who embody FIRST values â€” nominated by their team, two finalists per event.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a press release?", a:"Short formal announcement sent to local news about a team achievement or event â€” expands public awareness.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a team newsletter?", a:"Regular email/print update sent to sponsors, parents, and community partners sharing team news and achievements.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is workshop hosting?", a:"Running coding, CAD, or robotics workshops for students outside your team â€” high-impact outreach directly teaching STEM skills.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an FLL connection?", a:"Running or supporting First Lego League events introduces younger students to FIRST and builds a pipeline for FTC/FRC.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"What is an executive summary for Impact?", a:"Brief one-page overview covering the team's outreach philosophy and top three quantified impacts for the award application.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a FIRST team's annual report?", a:"Document summarizing the season's achievements, finances, outreach, and robot performance â€” shared with sponsors and partners.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is international outreach?", a:"Connecting with FIRST teams globally to share knowledge, mentor via video call, or support teams in under-resourced regions.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is diversity and inclusion outreach?", a:"Actively recruiting underrepresented groups into STEM and FIRST. Tracked and scored in Impact Award judging.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a sustainability plan?", a:"Strategy to maintain funding, membership, and mentors year-over-year so the team continues beyond any graduating class.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a corporate mentorship program?", a:"Arrangement where a sponsor company sends engineers to regularly mentor your team members in technical skills.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a sponsor tier structure?", a:"Categorized sponsorship levels (Gold, Silver, Bronze) with different recognition benefits per tier â€” simplifies the ask.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a social impact story?", a:"A specific, personal narrative of how a team's outreach changed someone's life â€” the most powerful tool in an Impact presentation.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a STEM career panel?", a:"Event where professionals talk with students about their careers â€” easily organized, high-impact, loved by judges.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is an outreach calendar?", a:"Planned schedule of outreach events for the entire season prepared in preseason â€” ensures consistent activity rather than last-minute scrambling.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW v6 ---
      { q:"What is a FIRST team number?", a:"A unique number assigned when a team registers with FIRST. It's permanent and used across all events and databases like The Blue Alliance.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a team website?", a:"A public-facing website sharing your team's story, robot reveals, outreach activities, and sponsor list. Essential for professional sponsor outreach.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a team T-shirt?", a:"Matching team apparel builds identity at events and in the community. Sponsor logos on shirts provide ongoing visibility â€” a good bargaining chip for sponsorships.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a pit display?", a:"A visual display in your competition pit showcasing team accomplishments, outreach photos, robot history, and sponsor logos. Judges visit pits during awards evaluation.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a mentor appreciation?", a:"Formally recognizing mentors (Woodie Flowers nomination, gifts, appreciation events) builds loyalty and retains experienced adults long-term.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is FIRST's 'For Inspiration' mission?", a:"FIRST aims to inspire young people to pursue STEM careers. All outreach and robot activities should connect to this mission when describing team impact.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a team portfolio?", a:"A curated collection of your best outreach photos, metrics, testimonials, and media coverage used in award submissions and sponsor proposals.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a 'Gracious Professional' moment?", a:"A documented story of exceptional sportsmanship or community helpfulness â€” powerful content for Impact Award essays and sponsor reports.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a community needs assessment?", a:"Researching what STEM education gaps exist locally before designing outreach programs â€” ensures your activities address real community needs.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a logic model for outreach?", a:"A visual framework mapping: Inputs â†’ Activities â†’ Outputs â†’ Outcomes â†’ Impact. Used in nonprofit planning to connect resources to long-term community change.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is school partnership outreach?", a:"Formal programs at local schools (weekly coding clubs, assembly visits, curriculum integration) â€” high-impact, recurring, and valued by FIRST judges.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a sponsor recognition event?", a:"An event (robot demo, open house, end-of-season party) inviting sponsors to see their investment in action â€” dramatically improves sponsor retention.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the FIRST Equity, Diversity & Inclusion initiative?", a:"FIRST's commitment to making robotics accessible to all students regardless of background. Teams with strong EDI programs score higher in Impact Award judging.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a digital media kit?", a:"A package of high-quality photos, logos, bios, and talking points provided to journalists or sponsors for easy media coverage of your team.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a theory of change?", a:"A clear articulation of how your team's activities lead to lasting community impact â€” required in a strong Impact Award essay.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is SMART goal-setting for outreach?", a:"Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound. 'Teach 200 students to code in Python by March 1' is SMART. 'Help kids learn coding' is not.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a program evaluation?", a:"Formally measuring whether an outreach program achieved its goals using surveys, pre/post tests, or tracking participants over time.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is earned media?", a:"Free press coverage (newspaper articles, TV segments, podcast features) about your team â€” more credible than paid advertising and valued in Impact submissions.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a 'multiplier effect' in outreach?", a:"When one of your trained students goes on to start a new FIRST team or STEM program, multiplying your team's impact beyond direct activities.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a partnership MOU for outreach?", a:"A formal written agreement with a school or organization defining each party's commitments for a joint STEM program â€” ensures accountability and longevity.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

  // â”€â”€â”€ 9. TEAM MANAGEMENT â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  teamManagement: {
    name: "Team Management",
    icon: "ðŸ‘¥",
    color: "#7c2d12",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"What is a team captain's role?", a:"Coordinate subteams, run meetings, resolve conflicts, communicate with mentors, and keep everyone aligned on season goals.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a kickoff meeting?", a:"First meeting after game reveal: analyze rules, brainstorm strategy, assign research tasks, set season-wide goals.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is subteam structure?", a:"Specialized groups (mechanical, electrical, programming, outreach) with a dedicated lead for each area.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a mentor's role?", a:"Guide students in problem-solving, teach skills, ensure safety â€” without doing the work for them.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a Kanban board?", a:"Visual board with columns (To Do, In Progress, Done). Trello or a physical whiteboard keeps everyone aligned.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is onboarding for new members?", a:"Structured introduction to team culture, tools, safety rules, and subteam workflows so new members contribute quickly.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a drive team?", a:"2â€“3 students operating the robot during matches (driver, operator, human player). Requires dedicated practice.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a pre-match checklist?", a:"Standardized list verified before every match: battery, mechanisms, wiring, correct code, controllers connected.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a team charter?", a:"Document defining mission, values, expectations, meeting schedules, and roles â€” sets norms from day one.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is conflict resolution?", a:"Addressing disagreements with active listening, finding common ground, and refocusing on shared goals.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What is a RACI matrix?", a:"Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed â€” clarifies who owns each task, who approves, and who needs updates.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Gantt chart?", a:"Project timeline with tasks as horizontal bars against a calendar. Used in build season to track milestones and dependencies.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a design review?", a:"Structured meeting evaluating a design for feasibility, reliability, and game strategy alignment before building.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is sprint planning?", a:"Breaking build season into 1â€“2 week sprints with specific goals. Keeps the team focused and allows frequent reassessment.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a retrospective?", a:"Post-competition review of what went well, what failed, and what the team will do differently next season.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is technical documentation?", a:"Written records of design decisions, code comments, wiring diagrams, and build logs. Critical for onboarding and awards.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an engineering notebook?", a:"Dated record of the team's design process, decisions, and testing. Scored in FIRST Impact and FTC Think/Design awards.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is effective meeting structure?", a:"Clear agenda, timekeeper, action item notes, end summary, preview of next meeting. Keeps meetings focused.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is delegation?", a:"Assigning tasks to specific people with clear expectations and deadlines â€” prevents bottlenecks, develops team members.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a team budget?", a:"Tracked plan of income vs. expected expenses. Prevents overspending on parts, registration, or travel.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a decision log?", a:"Record of major design or strategy decisions, who made them, and why. Invaluable for the engineering notebook.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is knowledge transfer?", a:"Documenting and teaching skills to new members so institutional knowledge doesn't leave with graduating seniors.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a build session log?", a:"Brief daily record of who attended, what was accomplished, and any blockers â€” feeds the engineering notebook.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a skills matrix?", a:"Table mapping team members to proficiencies (CAD, programming, machining) â€” identifies training gaps and informs task assignment.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"What is the critical path?", a:"Sequence of dependent tasks determining minimum project completion time. Delays here delay the whole project.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a 'stop and assess' week?", a:"Scheduled pause (often week 3 of 6) to honestly evaluate if the current design is meeting goals or needs a pivot.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is student leadership development?", a:"Intentionally mentoring students to lead meetings, train peers, and present to sponsors â€” a core team goal beyond robot building.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a project risk register?", a:"List of potential risks (key member absence, part shortage) with probability, impact, and mitigation plans.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a succession plan?", a:"A plan ensuring leadership roles are transitioned to new students before senior leaders graduate â€” prevents leadership vacuum.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a working agreement?", a:"Norms the team collectively agrees to follow: 'We will be on time', 'We will not talk over each other', 'We will ask for help when stuck'.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a code freeze?", a:"Period before competition where no new features are added â€” only bug fixes â€” to ensure robot code stability.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is transparent finances?", a:"Sharing the team budget and spending openly with all members and families â€” builds trust and teaches financial literacy.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a team constitution?", a:"Formal governing document describing team structure, election processes, conflict resolution procedures, and amendment process.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is an MOU?", a:"Memorandum of Understanding â€” written agreement with a school, sponsor, or partner defining expectations and resources.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW v6 ---
      { q:"What is a build season?", a:"The 6-week period (FRC) or ~8-week period (FTC) after game reveal where teams design, build, and program their competition robot.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a gracious professional team member?", a:"Someone who competes hard, helps others, and maintains respect regardless of outcomes â€” the ideal FIRST team member personality.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a pit crew?", a:"Team members responsible for robot repair and maintenance at competitions â€” must work quickly under pressure between qualification matches.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a scouting role on a team?", a:"Members dedicated to tracking other teams' robot performance during matches to inform alliance selection and strategy â€” critical for competitive success.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a team timeline?", a:"A week-by-week schedule from kickoff to competition defining what must be completed each week to finish the robot on time.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a 'done' definition?", a:"Clear criteria that a task is complete: code is merged, tested, and documented â€” not just 'kind of works'. Prevents perpetually unfinished tasks.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a team t-shirt order process?", a:"Planning shirt designs, quantities, sizes, and timing early (before season) so shirts arrive before the first competition.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a resource allocation?", a:"Deciding which team members work on which tasks based on skills, interest, and project priority â€” a key leadership responsibility.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an after-action review (AAR)?", a:"A structured debrief immediately after a match or event: what happened, why, what to do differently. Used by military and elite sports teams.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a team vision statement?", a:"A short, inspiring description of the future the team is working toward: 'To build a diverse STEM community where every student finds their passion.'", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an OKR?", a:"Objectives and Key Results â€” a goal-setting framework: Objective='Win district championship', Key Results='Top-8 seed, 90% auto success rate, 0 field failures'.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a lessons-learned document?", a:"A structured record of what went wrong and right each season. Reviewed at kickoff each year to avoid repeating mistakes.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a team sponsor meeting?", a:"A scheduled presentation to potential or current sponsors showing robot progress, outreach data, and financial needs. Requires preparation and professionalism.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a team communication platform?", a:"A tool for team-wide messaging: Slack, Discord, GroupMe. Separate channels for each subteam keeps communication organized.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a 'parking lot' in meetings?", a:"A list of off-topic items raised during a meeting that get tabled for later discussion â€” keeps the current meeting on track.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a SWOT analysis?", a:"Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats â€” strategic framework for evaluating team position at the start of a season.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is servant leadership?", a:"Leadership style focused on empowering and developing team members rather than directing them â€” the most effective style for FIRST team captains.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a team culture audit?", a:"A structured self-assessment of team culture: psychological safety, inclusion, communication quality, and alignment with values. Done annually.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a capacity plan?", a:"Forecasting how many labor-hours are available each week (accounting for school, exams, holidays) and matching work to that capacity.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is change management on a team?", a:"A deliberate process for introducing significant changes (new tools, restructured roles, new norms) with clear communication and time for adjustment.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

  // â”€â”€â”€ 10. SAFETY & SHOP RULES â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  safety: {
    name: "Safety & Shop Rules",
    icon: "ðŸ¦º",
    color: "#ca8a04",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"What PPE is required for power tools?", a:"Safety glasses always, hearing protection for loud tools, no loose clothing/jewelry. Closed-toe shoes required at all times.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a pinch point?", a:"Any location where a body part can be caught between moving parts â€” gears, belts, chains, shafts. Must be guarded.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"First step in any injury situation?", a:"Stop work, ensure area is safe, then help the injured person. Alert a mentor immediately. Never leave them alone.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is proper lifting technique?", a:"Bend at knees, keep load close to body, lift with legs not back, avoid twisting while carrying.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the emergency stop (E-stop)?", a:"Button on Driver Station that instantly disables the robot. Know its location before every practice run.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a safety data sheet (SDS)?", a:"Document for hazardous chemicals: safe handling, storage, PPE requirements, and emergency response.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a near-miss?", a:"An incident that almost caused injury. Always report it so the hazard can be fixed before someone gets hurt.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the buddy system in the shop?", a:"Never work alone in the shop. Always have at least one other person present for safety and emergency response.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a first aid kit?", a:"Stocked kit with bandages, antiseptic, burn cream, and gloves. Must be accessible and known to all team members.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"Danger of spinning mechanisms without guards?", a:"Exposed rotating parts can catch hair, fingers, or clothing instantly. Always guard or cage spinning components.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What is lockout/tagout (LOTO)?", a:"De-energize and physically lock equipment before maintenance â€” prevents accidental startup while servicing.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"Robot safety rule during testing?", a:"All members clear of robot's range of motion before enabling. One designated person calls 'clear' and controls the enable.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"Drill press safety rules?", a:"Clamp workpiece (never hand-hold), correct bit, remove chuck key before power-on, wear safety glasses.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"Electrical safety when wiring?", a:"Disconnect main battery before working on wiring. Verify off with multimeter. Tape exposed terminals.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What to do with metal chips/swarf?", a:"Never brush with bare hands â€” use a brush or cloth. Dispose in a designated sharps bin.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"3-foot rule for soldering?", a:"Keep all flammables 3+ feet from a soldering iron. Use a proper holder â€” never set a hot iron on a surface.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"Danger of LiPo batteries?", a:"Fire risk if punctured, overcharged, or short-circuited (thermal runaway). Store in fire-resistant bag; never charge unattended.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"Safe angle grinder use?", a:"Wear face shield and gloves, correct disc for material, keep guard in place, never use a cracked disc.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a robot perimeter safety zone?", a:"Marked boundary (typically 3â€“6 feet) around the robot during testing. Non-operators must stay behind it when robot is enabled.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"Safe bandsaw use?", a:"Keep fingers 1 inch from blade, use a fence or guide, never back out of a cut with the blade running.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"PPE for spray adhesives or paint?", a:"Nitrile gloves, safety glasses, and a respirator rated for organic vapors. Use outdoors or in a spray booth.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a fume extractor?", a:"Captures soldering smoke and chemical vapors at the source. Required for extended soldering sessions.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"When to use a fire extinguisher?", a:"Only if fire is small, you have a clear exit, and you're trained. PASS: Pull, Aim at base, Squeeze, Sweep.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"Chemical safety in the shop?", a:"Labeled containers, ventilated areas, never mix unknown chemicals, know the SDS for every substance.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"Safe table saw use?", a:"Use fence or miter gauge (never both), keep hands away from blade path, stand to the side, use a push stick for narrow cuts.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is safe use of compressed air?", a:"Never aim at a person. Wear eye protection. Check hose connections before use â€” leaks can be dangerous.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"Proper disposal of damaged batteries?", a:"Never in regular trash. Bring to a battery recycling center (AutoZone, Home Depot). Tape terminals to prevent short-circuit fires.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a hot work permit?", a:"Formal checklist/authorization required before welding, grinding, or soldering in facilities that have a hot work policy.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a safety captain?", a:"Designated team member responsible for safety culture: briefings, maintaining PPE supplies, and investigating near-misses.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a safety inspection at competition?", a:"FRC/FTC inspectors check your robot for unsafe wiring, sharp edges, unsecured batteries, and proper bumper installation.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is ergonomics in the shop?", a:"Setting up work surfaces at the correct height, taking breaks, and using proper posture to prevent repetitive strain injuries during long build sessions.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is slip/trip hazard prevention?", a:"Keep floors clear of cables, metal filings, tools, and scrap. Clean up spills immediately. Use cable covers for floor-crossing wires.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW v6 ---
      { q:"What is a safety briefing?", a:"A short presentation at the start of each work session covering active hazards, PPE requirements, and emergency procedures. Should take 2â€“3 minutes.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a safety poster?", a:"Visual reminders of rules posted in the shop: 'Safety glasses required beyond this point', 'Keep guards in place', 'No loose clothing'.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a burn from a motor/ESC?", a:"Motor controllers and stalled motors can become hot enough to cause burns. Touch metal housings carefully with the back of your hand before grabbing.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What are closed-toe shoes?", a:"Shoes fully covering all toes â€” required in all robotics shop environments. Sandals and flip-flops are never acceptable near tools or heavy components.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is tie-back for long hair?", a:"Long hair must be tied back or covered before using any rotating tool or being near a running robot. Hair can be pulled in instantly and cause severe injury.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the ring rule in the shop?", a:"Remove all rings, bracelets, and metal jewelry before working with electrical systems or rotating machinery â€” jewelry can cause shorts or entanglement.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a safety sign in the shop?", a:"Color-coded signs: Red=Danger (immediate hazard), Orange=Warning (potential hazard), Yellow=Caution (minor risk), Green=Safety information.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a safe work zone?", a:"A clearly defined and marked area around a hazard (running robot, power tool) where only authorized, trained people may stand.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a cut-resistant glove?", a:"A glove rated to resist cuts from sharp sheet metal or hardware. Required when handling freshly cut aluminum, steel edges, or sheet metal.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a respiratory hazard in the shop?", a:"Fine particulate from sanding, resin fumes from printing, soldering smoke, and spray chemicals all pose inhalation risks â€” use ventilation and appropriate respirators.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a grounding strap?", a:"A wrist strap connecting you to ground via a resistor â€” bleeds off static electricity when handling sensitive electronics like microcontrollers and motor controllers.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a tool inspection procedure?", a:"Before each use: check for damage, missing guards, frayed cords, and dull blades. Tag damaged tools 'OUT OF SERVICE' and remove from the shop floor.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a robot tether policy?", a:"Some teams use a tether (physical cable) between the Driver Station and robot during initial testing to guarantee immediate disable capability before radio is trusted.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a chemical inventory?", a:"A list of all hazardous substances in the shop (adhesives, lubricants, solvents) with SDS for each, stored in an accessible binder near the work area.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a voltage probe safety practice?", a:"Set multimeter to the expected voltage range BEFORE touching probes to a circuit. Touch the ground probe first, then the positive â€” reduces risk of arcing.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is an isolation transformer?", a:"A transformer with 1:1 ratio isolating a circuit from ground â€” provides shock protection when probing live circuits. Used in advanced electrical testing.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is arc flash hazard?", a:"An explosive release of energy from an electrical arc fault â€” rare in 12V robot systems but a real hazard around 120V tools and battery charging stations.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Job Safety Analysis (JSA)?", a:"A written document breaking a task into steps and identifying hazards at each step with controls. Required before any novel or high-risk fabrication operation.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a LOTO procedure for a robot?", a:"Disconnect battery, press E-stop, remove battery physically, and place a 'DO NOT ENERGIZE' tag before performing any maintenance on actuated robot systems.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is electrical safety PPE?", a:"Insulated gloves (rated for voltage), safety glasses, and non-conductive footwear when working on live circuits above 50V. Always use rated PPE for the voltage present.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

  // â”€â”€â”€ 11. FIRST AWARDS â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  awards: {
    name: "FIRST Awards",
    icon: "ðŸ†",
    color: "#d97706",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"What is the Impact Award?", a:"FIRST's highest honor â€” given to the team best embodying FIRST's mission with the most significant, sustained community impact.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the Spirit Award?", a:"Recognizes a team exemplifying FIRST spirit through enthusiasm, teamwork, and gracious professionalism throughout the event.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the Highest Rookie Seed Award?", a:"Given to the highest-seeded first-year team at end of qualifications. Recognizes strong performance by a new team.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the Rookie All-Star Award?", a:"Given to the first-year team best exemplifying rookie effort, spirit, and performance â€” leads to Impact Award consideration.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the Gracious Professionalism Award?", a:"Recognizes a team consistently demonstrating respect, cooperation, and collaborative spirit on and off the field.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the Safety Award?", a:"Recognizes a team with a comprehensive safety program and safety-first culture throughout their team and shop.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the Inspire Award in FTC?", a:"The top FTC award â€” equivalent to Impact Award in FRC. Given to the team that best represents the essence of the FIRST mission.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the Judges' Award?", a:"Discretionary award for a team with a unique quality not captured by other awards â€” fully at judges' discretion.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What replaced the Chairman's Award?", a:"The Impact Award (renamed 2022) â€” same criteria, emphasizing measurable community and STEM education impact.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Engineering Inspiration Award?", a:"Recognizes a team excelling at spreading FIRST values and STEM enthusiasm into their school and community.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Woodie Flowers Finalist Award?", a:"Honors a mentor using empathy, communication, and passion to make engineering accessible. Nominated by their own team.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Dean's List Award?", a:"Recognizes up to two exceptional student leaders per event who embody FIRST values â€” nominated by their team.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Excellence in Engineering Award?", a:"Celebrates an elegant, efficient, creative solution â€” outstanding engineering design and execution on the robot.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Quality Award?", a:"Recognizes a robot demonstrating durability, robustness, and attention to detail in construction.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Imagery Award?", a:"Given to the team combining creativity and design best in their robot, uniforms, and display to communicate their team theme.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Innovation in Control Award?", a:"Recognizes creative and innovative use of technology in the control system, sensors, or software.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Industrial Design Award?", a:"Given to a team whose robot reflects a professional design process considering aesthetics, human factors, and design intent.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Think Award in FTC?", a:"Recognizes the team that best reflects their engineering process journey in their engineering notebook.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Design Award in FTC?", a:"Recognizes the most elegant and well-designed robot â€” design choices driven by game strategy.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Control Award in FTC?", a:"Recognizes the most elegant and effective sensor-based solution to a challenge encountered during the season.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Motivate Award in FTC?", a:"Recognizes the team that spreads FIRST values the most and creates the most diverse, inclusive team and community.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"How are judged awards decided?", a:"Trained judge panel interviews teams, reviews engineering notebooks, and deliberates per each award's criteria.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"What does Impact Award submission require?", a:"Written essay (10,000 char), executive summary, live judging presentation, and quantified outreach data.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is the Entrepreneurship Award?", a:"Recognizes a team with a comprehensive business plan detailing financial model, sustainability strategy, and community outreach.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is award eligibility at championships?", a:"Teams winning specific awards at regionals/districts advance to championships to compete for the same award globally.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a judging interview?", a:"5â€“10 minute session presenting work to award judges and answering questions. Preparation and rehearsal are critical.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a team's award strategy?", a:"Identifying 2â€“3 awards aligning best with team strengths, then investing documentation and preparation specifically for those.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is the Impact Award essay structure?", a:"Cover: who you are, theory of change, top impacts (quantified), sustainability, and call to action â€” all in â‰¤10,000 characters.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is the 'story' in an Impact presentation?", a:"Compelling narrative showing the team's journey, why they do outreach, and concrete evidence that lives were changed.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is 'sustainable impact' in award judging?", a:"Impact that continues after the team's direct involvement â€” trained students who go on to build new teams, programs that outlast the season.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a judging rubric?", a:"FIRST publishes rubrics for awards like Impact and Innovation in Control. Teams should study and address every criterion.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is an award callback?", a:"When judges request a second interview â€” a strong signal that you're a serious contender for that award.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW v6 ---
      { q:"What is a FIRST event?", a:"A sanctioned robotics competition where teams demonstrate their robots and are evaluated for both performance and non-performance awards by judges.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a judging session?", a:"A scheduled meeting between your team and a panel of trained volunteer judges who evaluate your team for non-performance awards.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a team photo for awards?", a:"A formal photo of the whole team used in award submissions, press releases, and engineering notebooks. Take it early in the season.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is an engineering portfolio?", a:"A binder or digital document presented to judges containing your notebook, CAD drawings, code samples, and design documentation.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the 'Rookie Year' of a team?", a:"The first season a team competes. Rookie teams are eligible for special awards and are often treated with extra encouragement by the FIRST community.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is an award ceremony at a FIRST event?", a:"The closing ceremony where all non-performance and performance awards are announced. All team members should attend in full team apparel.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the Autonomous Award in FTC?", a:"Recognizes the team with the best autonomous period strategy and execution â€” judged by performance data and notebook documentation of the auto process.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Connect Award in FTC?", a:"Recognizes a team connecting with their local engineering and technology community through meaningful, documented relationships.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Promote Award in FTC?", a:"Recognizes a team that creates a video advocating for FIRST â€” judged on creativity and effectiveness at inspiring others to join.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Sustainability Award in FTC?", a:"Recognizes FTC teams with a strong plan to sustain their team through fundraising, community support, and leadership development.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a peer-nominated award?", a:"An award where other teams (not judges) vote â€” like the Imagery Award at some events. Requires visible branding and a positive team reputation.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Entrepreneurship Award in FRC?", a:"Recognizes a team with a comprehensive business plan detailing financial model, community outreach strategy, and team sustainability plan.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a judge's deliberation process?", a:"Judges compare teams against award rubrics in a closed meeting after all interviews. They must reach consensus â€” teams never see deliberation notes.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an award callback?", a:"When judges request a second interview or additional information â€” a strong signal you're a serious contender for that award.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Collins Aerospace Innovate Award?", a:"An FRC award sponsored by Collins Aerospace recognizing teams for creativity and innovation in an industrial or professional engineering context.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an award-winning notebook structure?", a:"Date every entry, include photos, record decisions AND the reasons behind them, show failed attempts, and reference specific game objectives throughout.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a 'killer app' for the Impact Award?", a:"One flagship program that uniquely represents your team's outreach philosophy â€” judges remember specific, distinctive programs better than a long list of events.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is the 10,000-character limit for Impact?", a:"The essay must be under 10,000 characters (not words). Precision matters â€” every sentence must add unique value. Teams typically write 3â€“5 drafts.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a pre-scouted judge?", a:"Some teams research judges' professional backgrounds to tailor their presentation to the judges' expertise â€” e.g., using engineering language with an engineering judge.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a mock judging session?", a:"Practicing your judging presentation with mentors or other teams acting as judges â€” timed, with realistic Q&A to prepare for real judging pressure.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

  // â”€â”€â”€ 12. HTML & WEB DEVELOPMENT â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  webDev: {
    name: "HTML & Web Development",
    icon: "ðŸŒ",
    color: "#0e7490",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"What is HTML?", a:"HyperText Markup Language â€” standard language for web page structure and content using nested tags.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a HTML tag?", a:"Element in angle brackets: <p>, <div>, <h1>. Most have opening and closing tags. Self-closing: <img />, <input />.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is DOCTYPE?", a:"<!DOCTYPE html> tells the browser to use modern HTML5 parsing rules. Must be the very first line of the file.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"<div> vs. <span>?", a:"<div> is block-level (full width, new line). <span> is inline (wraps text). Both are generic containers for CSS/JS.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is CSS?", a:"Cascading Style Sheets â€” controls visual presentation (colors, fonts, layout, spacing) of HTML elements.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a CSS selector?", a:"Targets elements to style: tag (p {}), class (.card {}), ID (#header {}), attribute, pseudo-class (:hover).", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"class vs. ID in CSS?", a:"IDs (#) must be unique per page. Classes (.) can be reused. IDs have higher specificity than classes.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is JavaScript?", a:"Scripting language running in the browser â€” makes pages interactive via events, DOM manipulation, and API calls.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is JSON?", a:"JavaScript Object Notation â€” lightweight text data format: {\"key\": \"value\"}. Used in all web APIs and config files.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the DOM?", a:"Document Object Model â€” a tree representation of the HTML page that JavaScript can read and modify dynamically.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What does getElementById() do?", a:"Returns the element with the given ID so JavaScript can read or modify its content, style, or attributes.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is an event listener?", a:"element.addEventListener('click', handler). Attaches a function triggered by a browser event â€” foundation of interactive UIs.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is semantic HTML?", a:"Elements with meaning: <header>, <nav>, <main>, <section>, <article>, <footer>. Improves accessibility, SEO, readability.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What is the CSS box model?", a:"Every element: content â†’ padding â†’ border â†’ margin. Controls all spacing and sizing on the page.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is Flexbox?", a:"display: flex on a container controls how children align (align-items) and distribute (justify-content) along axes.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is CSS Grid?", a:"2D layout with rows and columns: display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr. Positions elements precisely.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is fetch()?", a:"Browser API for HTTP requests: fetch(url).then(r => r.json()).then(data => ...). Used to call REST APIs like TBA.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a REST API?", a:"Architectural style: clients make HTTP requests (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) to endpoints returning JSON data.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is responsive design?", a:"Layout adapts to different screen sizes using CSS media queries, Flexbox/Grid, and relative units.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a media query?", a:"@media (max-width: 768px) { ... } â€” applies styles only when conditions are met. Foundation of mobile-responsive design.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"GET vs. POST?", a:"GET retrieves data (params in URL, cacheable). POST sends data in request body â€” used for form submissions and creating resources.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a CSS transition?", a:"transition: all 0.3s ease â€” smoothly animates CSS property changes like hover effects without JavaScript keyframes.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is localStorage?", a:"Browser API storing key-value strings persistently: localStorage.setItem('key','val'), .getItem('key'). Survives page refresh.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is npm?", a:"Node Package Manager â€” installs JavaScript libraries. Key commands: npm install, npm run start, npm run build.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a CSS custom property?", a:":root { --primary: #1d4ed8; } used as color: var(--primary). Makes global theme changes easy to manage.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is Tailwind CSS?", a:"Utility-first framework: style by composing small utility classes (bg-blue-500, p-4, flex) directly in HTML markup.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a SPA?", a:"Single Page Application â€” loads one HTML page and dynamically updates content via JavaScript without full page reloads.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is debouncing in JavaScript?", a:"Delaying a function call until after the user stops triggering it. Used for search boxes to avoid firing an API call on every keystroke.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"What is React?", a:"JavaScript library for building UIs with reusable components. Components return JSX and manage state via hooks.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is useState?", a:"const [value, setValue] = useState(initial). Calling setValue triggers a re-render with the new value.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is useEffect in React?", a:"useEffect(() => { fetchData(); }, [dep]). Runs side effects after render; re-runs when dependency array changes.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is async/await in JavaScript?", a:"async function getData() { const res = await fetch(url); const data = await res.json(); }. Reads like synchronous code.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Promise?", a:"Object representing an eventual value. States: pending â†’ fulfilled or rejected. Chain with .then()/.catch() or use async/await.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is CORS?", a:"Cross-Origin Resource Sharing â€” browser blocks requests to different domains. APIs must include CORS headers to be accessible.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is TypeScript?", a:"JavaScript superset adding static type annotations. Types catch bugs at compile time rather than at runtime.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a webpack/bundler?", a:"Tool bundling multiple JS/CSS files into optimized output files for the browser. Webpack, Vite, and Parcel are common bundlers.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is server-side rendering (SSR)?", a:"HTML generated on the server (faster first paint, better SEO) vs. client-side rendering (HTML generated in browser via JavaScript).", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a 404 vs. 500 error?", a:"404: resource not found (client error). 500: internal server error (server crash). 200=OK, 201=created, 401=unauthorized.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW v6 ---
      { q:"What is a web browser?", a:"Software that renders HTML, CSS, and JavaScript into visual web pages: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge. Each has developer tools (F12) for debugging.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a URL?", a:"Uniform Resource Locator â€” the address of a web resource: https://www.google.com/search?q=FRC. Contains protocol, domain, path, and optional query string.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is an HTML attribute?", a:"Extra information inside an opening tag: <img src=\"robot.jpg\" alt=\"Robot\">. Common attributes: id, class, src, href, type, placeholder.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a hyperlink in HTML?", a:"<a href=\"https://firstinspires.org\">Click here</a>. The href attribute sets the destination. target=\"_blank\" opens in a new tab.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is an HTML form?", a:"A UI element collecting user input: <form> contains <input>, <select>, <textarea>, and <button> elements. Data is sent to a server or handled by JavaScript.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is inline vs. external CSS?", a:"Inline: style attribute on an element. Internal: <style> tag in <head>. External: separate .css file linked with <link>. External is best for maintainability.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a font in CSS?", a:"font-family: 'Arial', sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: bold. Google Fonts provides hundreds of free web fonts via a <link> import.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is z-index in CSS?", a:"Controls stacking order of overlapping elements. Higher z-index renders on top. Only works on positioned elements (position: relative/absolute/fixed).", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is CSS position: absolute vs relative?", a:"Relative: offset from its normal position. Absolute: positioned relative to nearest positioned ancestor, removed from normal flow. Fixed: relative to viewport.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a CSS pseudo-element?", a:"::before and ::after inject content before/after an element's content. Used for decorative elements and clearfixes: .card::before { content: ''; }.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Web Worker?", a:"A JavaScript thread running in the background without blocking the UI. Used for heavy computation (image processing, data analysis) to keep the page responsive.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the Intersection Observer API?", a:"Browser API detecting when an element enters or exits the viewport â€” used for lazy loading images and triggering scroll-based animations.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a content security policy (CSP)?", a:"An HTTP header restricting which scripts, styles, and resources a page can load â€” primary defense against cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a service worker?", a:"A script running in the background enabling offline caching, push notifications, and background sync for Progressive Web Apps (PWAs).", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is React Context?", a:"const Ctx = createContext(); provides global state accessible to any component without prop drilling. Wrap the app in <Ctx.Provider value={data}>.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is useCallback in React?", a:"useCallback(fn, [deps]) memoizes a function reference â€” prevents child components from re-rendering when the parent re-renders if the deps haven't changed.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is code splitting in React?", a:"const Comp = React.lazy(() => import('./Heavy')). Loads components on demand, reducing initial bundle size and improving first-load performance.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a virtual DOM?", a:"React maintains a lightweight copy of the DOM in memory. On state change it diffs the virtual DOM and applies only minimal real DOM updates â€” fast rendering.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is WebSocket?", a:"A protocol providing full-duplex communication over a single TCP connection: const ws = new WebSocket('wss://server'). Used for real-time dashboards and live scouting apps.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is tree shaking in JavaScript?", a:"Dead code elimination during bundling â€” unused exports are removed from the final bundle. Requires ES modules (import/export). Reduces bundle size significantly.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },
