  // â”€â”€â”€ 13. FRC SPECIFIC â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  frc: {
    name: "FRC Specific",
    icon: "ðŸ¤–",
    color: "#1e40af",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"What is FRC?", a:"FIRST Robotics Competition â€” annual high school robotics competition where teams of 25+ students build a robot in 6 weeks to compete.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the RoboRIO?", a:"Main FRC robot controller â€” Linux-based National Instruments computer running robot code and interfacing with all hardware.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the Driver Station software?", a:"PC application controlling robot enable/disable, sending joystick data, and displaying robot diagnostics during matches.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is FMS?", a:"Field Management System â€” hardware/software managing match timing, team communication, robot enable/disable, and score recording.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a bumper in FRC?", a:"Mandatory robot perimeter covering made of pool noodles and plywood wrapped in fabric. Must meet strict FIRST rules.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the FRC weight limit?", a:"125 lbs for the robot (excluding bumpers and battery) in most recent seasons. Teams weigh-in at events.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is WPILib?", a:"Official FRC programming library for Java/C++. Provides hardware wrappers, Command-Based framework, PID, trajectory following, and simulation.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a SparkMAX?", a:"REV Robotics FRC motor controller for brushless (NEO, NEO 550) and brushed motors. Supports CAN and PWM.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is SmartDashboard / Shuffleboard?", a:"WPILib dashboard tools. SmartDashboard is simpler; Shuffleboard has drag-and-drop widgets, graphs, and camera feeds.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a CAN ID?", a:"Unique number (0â€“62) assigned to each CAN bus device. Each motor controller and sensor must have a distinct CAN ID.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What is the Command-Based framework?", a:"WPILib design pattern organizing code into Commands (actions) and Subsystems (hardware groups). Commands are scheduled automatically.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Subsystem in WPILib?", a:"Class extending SubsystemBase representing one hardware group (Drivetrain, Intake). Has periodic() called every 20ms loop.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Command in WPILib?", a:"An action a Subsystem performs. Has initialize(), execute(), isFinished(), and end(). Requires specific Subsystems to prevent conflicts.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is Network Tables?", a:"Distributed key-value pub/sub system allowing the robot, Driver Station, coprocessors, and dashboards to share data over the network.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is Limelight?", a:"Plug-and-play FRC vision system with onboard processing running pre-built targeting pipelines. Simple Network Tables integration.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What are AprilTags in FRC?", a:"QR-code-like fiducial markers on the FRC field. Cameras detect them to calculate the robot's precise field position and heading.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is PathPlanner?", a:"Popular FRC autonomous path-planning GUI generating trajectories that integrate with WPILib or PathPlanner's own controller.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a NavX / Pigeon IMU?", a:"Common FRC gyroscopes/IMUs providing 3-axis heading, pitch, roll. Used for field-centric drive and auto heading correction.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a ratchet mechanism in FRC?", a:"One-way mechanical stop allowing rotation in one direction only. Used in climbers to hold position without motor power.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a TalonSRX/FX?", a:"CTRE motor controllers over CAN. TalonFX has built-in Falcon 500 motor. Supports PID, Motion Magic, and sensor fusion.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an FRC inspection checklist?", a:"Official list verifying robot weight, size, bumper compliance, safety features, and electrical standards before a team can compete.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is PhotonVision?", a:"Open-source FRC vision software running on a coprocessor. Detects AprilTags and retroreflective targets for pose estimation.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"What is AdvantageKit?", a:"FRC data logging and replay framework recording all inputs so you can replay a match in simulation to debug code issues.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is Motion Magic (CTRE)?", a:"Closed-loop mode automatically generating a trapezoidal motion profile to reach a target position at controlled speed and acceleration.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a swerve drive kinematics class?", a:"WPILib's SwerveDriveKinematics converts chassis speeds (vx, vy, Ï‰) into individual module states (wheel speed + steering angle).", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is pose estimation in FRC?", a:"Fusing wheel odometry with vision measurements (AprilTags) to track the robot's position on the field with high accuracy.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a command scheduler?", a:"WPILib's CommandScheduler runs all active commands each loop, checking isFinished(), resolving requirements conflicts, and calling end().", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a trigger in Command-Based?", a:"A Trigger binds a condition (button press, sensor threshold) to a command: button.onTrue(new IntakeCommand()).", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a SequentialCommandGroup?", a:"A WPILib command that runs multiple commands one after another â€” foundational building block for autonomous routines.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is Choreo?", a:"FRC trajectory optimization tool generating time-optimal paths respecting robot physical constraints â€” more accurate than simple splines.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a CTRE CANcoder?", a:"Absolute magnetic encoder by CTRE communicating over CAN. Commonly used for swerve module steering angle measurement.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a roboRIO watchdog?", a:"Hardware timer that resets the roboRIO if software freezes or the control loop takes too long â€” ensures the robot can always be disabled.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW v6 ---
      { q:"What is a FIRST season kickoff?", a:"The day in January when the new FRC game is revealed globally. Teams receive the game manual, field drawings, and kit of parts simultaneously worldwide.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a kit of parts?", a:"A standardized set of components distributed to all FRC teams at kickoff including motors, controllers, and structural elements to ensure a baseline of accessibility.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a practice match?", a:"An unofficial match at events allowing teams to test robot performance in field conditions before qualification matches begin.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a pit at an FRC event?", a:"A designated workspace for each team in the pit area where the robot is stored, repaired, and prepared between matches during competition.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a field element?", a:"The physical structures on the competition field that robots interact with: goals, game piece dispensers, climbing structures, gates, etc.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is robot weigh-in?", a:"An official measurement of robot weight at inspection. The robot (without battery and bumpers) must be under 125 lbs. Failed weigh-in means removing parts.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a district point system?", a:"FRC district teams earn points at events based on seeding, playoff advancement, and awards. Top point-earners qualify for the District Championship.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a hall-effect absolute encoder in FRC?", a:"A sensor (e.g., CANcoder) using magnets to report absolute shaft position (0â€“360Â°) every power cycle â€” eliminates the need to home mechanisms after each enable.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is REV's SPARK Flex?", a:"An updated REV brushless motor controller supporting the Vortex motor. Compact, can run in attached or remote configurations with CAN or PWM.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a vision pipeline latency?", a:"The delay between when a camera sees a target and when the robot code receives the data. High latency (>100ms) degrades targeting accuracy at high speed.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a WPILib simulation?", a:"The ability to run robot code on a desktop PC with simulated hardware â€” test autonomous routines and logic without a physical robot present.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a robot characterization voltage ramp test?", a:"SysId applies a slowly increasing voltage to a mechanism while recording position and velocity to calculate feedforward constants (kS, kV, kA) accurately.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Ramsete controller?", a:"A WPILib path-following controller for differential drive robots that corrects both positional and heading error to follow a planned trajectory accurately.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Swerve Drive Specialties (SDS) module?", a:"A popular COTS FRC swerve module from SDS available in multiple gear ratios. Widely used by teams building swerve drivetrains for the first time.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a pose2d in WPILib?", a:"A data class representing a 2D robot pose: Pose2d(x_meters, y_meters, rotation2d). Used throughout WPILib for odometry, path following, and vision.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a DifferentialDriveOdometry?", a:"WPILib class tracking a tank drive robot's position using left/right encoder deltas and gyro heading: odometry.update(gyroAngle, leftMeters, rightMeters).", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Profiled PID Controller?", a:"A WPILib PID controller with built-in trapezoidal motion profile â€” automatically limits velocity and acceleration to avoid overshoot and mechanical stress.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a NT4 (Network Tables v4)?", a:"The latest Network Tables protocol used in WPILib 2023+. Faster, more efficient, supports timestamps and better publisher/subscriber semantics than NT3.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a rotation2d in WPILib?", a:"A class representing a 2D rotation: Rotation2d.fromDegrees(90). Handles angle wrapping and arithmetic correctly â€” always use it instead of raw doubles for headings.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a feedforward model for a flywheel?", a:"voltage = kS * Math.signum(velocity) + kV * velocity + kA * acceleration. kS overcomes static friction; kV maintains speed; kA provides acceleration torque.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

  // â”€â”€â”€ 14. MATH & PHYSICS â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  mathPhysics: {
    name: "Math & Physics",
    icon: "ðŸ“Š",
    color: "#4f46e5",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"What is torque?", a:"Rotational force = Force Ã— moment arm. Units: NÂ·m or ozÂ·in. Stall torque is maximum torque at zero speed.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is Newton's Second Law?", a:"F = m Ã— a. Heavier robots require more force to accelerate at the same rate.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is friction force?", a:"F_friction = Î¼ Ã— F_normal. The friction coefficient Î¼ determines how much lateral force a wheel can exert before slipping.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a free body diagram?", a:"Diagram showing all forces on an object (gravity, normal, applied, friction). Used to analyze mechanism loads.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is mechanical advantage?", a:"Output force / input force. A pulley or gear reducing speed multiplies force by the same ratio.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the unit circle?", a:"Circle of radius 1 defining sin and cos for any angle. Used everywhere in robotics: heading math, motor mixing, swerve kinematics.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is encoder tick-to-distance?", a:"distance = ticks Ã— (wheel_circumference / ticks_per_revolution). Converts encoder readings to real-world units.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is angular velocity?", a:"Rotational speed in rad/s or RPM. Ï‰ = 2Ï€ Ã— RPM / 60. Related to linear velocity by v = Ï‰ Ã— radius.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a deadband?", a:"Range around zero input (e.g., Â±0.05) where motor power is set to zero. Prevents joystick drift from causing unwanted movement.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What is PID math?", a:"Output = KpÃ—error + KiÃ—âˆ«error dt + KdÃ—(d error/dt). P drives toward setpoint; I removes steady-state error; D damps oscillation.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a trapezoidal motion profile?", a:"Accelerate at max accel â†’ cruise at max velocity â†’ decelerate to stop. Smoothly reaches target without overshoot.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is linear interpolation (lerp)?", a:"lerp(a, b, t) = a + tÃ—(b-a). Smoothly transitions between two values at fraction t (0â€“1). Used for motor ramping.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a vector?", a:"Quantity with magnitude and direction: velocity = (vx, vy). Added component-wise. Used in mecanum and swerve math.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a rotation matrix?", a:"2Ã—2 matrix rotating a 2D vector by angle Î¸: [cosÎ¸, -sinÎ¸; sinÎ¸, cosÎ¸]. Converts field-relative to robot-relative vectors.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is centripetal acceleration?", a:"a = vÂ²/r. Acceleration toward center of circular path. Affects stability when turning at high speed with a high COG.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is gear efficiency?", a:"Power lost in each gear mesh (~95-98% per stage). A 3-stage gearbox is ~85-94% efficient overall.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is odometry math?", a:"Î”x = Î”forwardÃ—cos(Î¸) - Î”strafeÃ—sin(Î¸), Î”y = Î”forwardÃ—sin(Î¸) + Î”strafeÃ—cos(Î¸). Integrates encoder data into position.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is moment of inertia (I)?", a:"I = Î£(m Ã— rÂ²). Resistance to rotational acceleration. Larger radius = higher I = harder to spin up.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is Hooke's Law?", a:"F = k Ã— x. Force equals spring constant times displacement. Used to model compliant intake forces and spring preload.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"Torque and power relationship?", a:"P = Ï„ Ã— Ï‰. Power (watts) = torque (NÂ·m) Ã— angular velocity (rad/s). Peak power is at ~50% of free-run speed.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is projectile motion?", a:"Under gravity only: horizontal velocity constant, vertical decelerates at 9.8 m/sÂ². Used for ball launcher design.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"What is a Bezier curve?", a:"Smooth parametric curve defined by control points. Used in autonomous path planning (Road Runner, PathPlanner) for smooth trajectories.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is the small angle approximation?", a:"For angles < ~15Â°: sinÎ¸ â‰ˆ Î¸, cosÎ¸ â‰ˆ 1, tanÎ¸ â‰ˆ Î¸ (radians). Simplifies rotation math in vision and odometry code.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a cross product?", a:"A Ã— B = |A||B|sinÎ¸, perpendicular to both inputs. Used in 3D robotics to calculate torques and angular velocities.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a least-squares solution?", a:"Finds best-fit x in Ax = b when overdetermined. Used to calculate OPR from match data: np.linalg.lstsq().", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a state-space model?", a:"Mathematical model using state vectors (position, velocity) and state transition matrices. Foundation for advanced robot control (LQR).", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is an LQR controller?", a:"Linear Quadratic Regulator â€” optimal controller minimizing a cost function balancing state error and control effort.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Kalman filter?", a:"Algorithm fusing noisy sensor measurements with a model prediction to produce a better state estimate. Used for pose estimation.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a feedforward term?", a:"Model-based term added to control output to predict required input: voltage = kS + kVÃ—velocity + kAÃ—acceleration.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is dimensional analysis?", a:"Tracking units through calculations to verify correctness. E.g., (ticks/rev) Ã— (rev/in)â»Â¹ â†’ ticks per inch.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a gradient descent?", a:"Optimization algorithm minimizing a cost function by iteratively stepping in the direction of steepest descent. Used in ML training and some tuning tools.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW v6 ---
      { q:"What is addition vs. multiplication in real life?", a:"Adding forces: two parallel forces combined. Multiplying: force Ã— distance = torque, mass Ã— acceleration = force. Understanding which applies is fundamental to mechanism design.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a ratio?", a:"A comparison of two quantities: 3:1 gear ratio means input turns 3Ã— for every 1 output turn. Ratios are everywhere in robotics â€” motors, pulleys, sprockets.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is speed vs. velocity?", a:"Speed is magnitude only (5 m/s). Velocity includes direction (5 m/s north). In robotics, velocity is a vector while speed is a scalar.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is acceleration?", a:"Rate of change of velocity: a = Î”v/Î”t. Units: m/sÂ². A robot accelerating from 0 to 3 m/s in 0.5s has a = 6 m/sÂ².", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is gravity?", a:"9.8 m/sÂ² downward acceleration near Earth's surface. Weight = mass Ã— 9.8. A 5 kg arm experiences 49 N of gravitational force at its center of mass.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is the Pythagorean theorem in robotics?", a:"aÂ² + bÂ² = cÂ². Used to find distances on the field, hypotenuse lengths in mechanism geometry, and vector magnitudes: |v| = âˆš(vxÂ²+vyÂ²).", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is sin and cos used for in robotics?", a:"sin(Î¸) and cos(Î¸) convert angles to x/y components. If a 1m arm is at 30Â°: x = cos(30Â°)=0.866m, y = sin(30Â°)=0.5m.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a coordinate system in FRC?", a:"FRC uses a field-centric coordinate system with X pointing away from the blue alliance wall and Y pointing left. Angles are measured counter-clockwise from +X.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is numerical integration?", a:"Approximating an integral by summing small steps: âˆ«f(x)dx â‰ˆ Î£ f(xáµ¢)Î”x. Used in odometry: position += velocity Ã— Î”t each loop iteration.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a unit vector?", a:"A vector of magnitude exactly 1 pointing in a specific direction. Normalize any vector: Ã» = v / |v|. Used in swerve and mecanum to separate direction from speed.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a polar coordinate?", a:"Represents a point as (r, Î¸) â€” distance from origin and angle â€” instead of (x, y). Useful for circular path planning and turret targeting.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a transfer function?", a:"A mathematical model relating system input to output in the frequency domain â€” used in control theory to analyze stability and design PID gains.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a step response?", a:"A system's reaction to a sudden input change (step). Characterized by rise time, overshoot %, settling time, and steady-state error â€” used to evaluate PID tuning.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is interpolation vs. extrapolation?", a:"Interpolation estimates values within a known data range. Extrapolation estimates beyond the range â€” less reliable. Shooter lookup tables use interpolation.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an eigenvalue?", a:"For a matrix A, eigenvalue Î» satisfies Av = Î»v. In state-space control, eigenvalues of the closed-loop system determine stability â€” negative real parts = stable.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Jacobian matrix?", a:"Matrix of partial derivatives relating joint velocities to end-effector velocities in a multi-joint arm. J * qÌ‡ = áº‹. Used for inverse kinematics and arm control.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is inverse kinematics?", a:"Computing joint angles needed to place an end-effector (gripper) at a desired position. Opposite of forward kinematics. Solved analytically or numerically.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Lyapunov stability proof?", a:"A mathematical technique proving a control system is stable by finding a Lyapunov function V(x) > 0 whose derivative dV/dt < 0 â€” guarantees convergence to equilibrium.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Fourier transform?", a:"Decomposes a signal into its frequency components. Used in vibration analysis to identify resonance frequencies in robot mechanisms that cause structural failure.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is model predictive control (MPC)?", a:"Optimizes control inputs over a future horizon by solving an optimization problem at each timestep. More computationally expensive than PID but handles constraints explicitly.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

  // â”€â”€â”€ 15. MOTORS & BATTERIES â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  motorsBatteries: {
    name: "Motors & Batteries",
    icon: "ðŸ”‹",
    color: "#065f46",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"What is a brushed DC motor?", a:"Uses physical brushes to transfer current to the spinning armature. Simple, inexpensive, but brushes wear and create friction.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is free speed?", a:"RPM a motor spins at with no load (zero torque). Actual operating speed is between free speed and stall depending on load.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a 12V SLA battery?", a:"Sealed Lead Acid â€” standard FRC battery. ~18 Ah capacity, heavy (~6 lbs), reliable. Must be charged with a proper smart charger.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"Brake mode vs. coast mode?", a:"Brake mode: motor actively resists motion when power is removed (better position holding). Coast mode: motor freewheels when power is removed.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"Servo vs. DC motor?", a:"Servos are geared motors with built-in position feedback â€” move to commanded angles. DC motors run continuously requiring external control.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is duty cycle?", a:"Percentage of time a motor is powered in a PWM signal. 100% = full power; 50% = half power; 0% = off.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a REV Slim Battery?", a:"FTC's standard 12V NiMH battery (3000 mAh). Lighter than SLA. FTC rules specify approved battery models.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is battery charging best practice?", a:"Use manufacturer-specified smart charger. Never charge at more than 1C. Remove from charger when full.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a gear reduction?", a:"Gear ratio reducing speed and increasing torque. A planetary gearbox is compact and commonly used in FRC/FTC.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What is a brushless motor?", a:"Uses electronic commutation instead of brushes. More efficient, longer lifespan, higher power density. Used in Falcon 500, NEO, Kraken.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a NEO motor?", a:"REV brushless FRC motor with built-in encoder, designed for SparkMAX. 6,380 RPM free speed, ~3.36 NÂ·m stall torque at 12V.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Falcon 500?", a:"Brushless FRC motor with integrated TalonFX controller and encoder. 6,380 RPM free, 4.69 NÂ·m stall torque. Popular in FRC drivetrains.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is stall torque?", a:"Maximum torque a motor produces at zero speed. At stall, current is also at maximum â€” can damage motor windings.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is stall current?", a:"Current drawn when a motor is completely stopped against a load. Very high â€” can trip breakers and burn out windings.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a motor's power curve?", a:"Graph of power vs. speed. Peak power occurs at ~50% of free speed. Choose gear ratio to operate near this point.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is smart current limiting?", a:"Software in SparkMAX/TalonFX limits motor current to prevent breaker trips and motor burnout. Typically ~80% of breaker rating.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a planetary gearbox?", a:"Compact gearbox with sun gear, planet gears, and ring gear. High reduction ratios, backdrivable, compact size.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is the UltraPlanetary gearbox?", a:"REV's modular FTC planetary gearbox with interchangeable cartridges (3:1, 4:1, 5:1). Up to 125:1 when stacked.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is battery internal resistance?", a:"Resistance inside the battery itself. Increases with age â€” causes more voltage sag under load. Test regularly.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a REV HD Hex Motor?", a:"Common FTC brushed motor at 6,000 RPM free speed with 2240 ticks/rev encoder. Used in slides, arms, and drivetrains.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a battery voltage tester?", a:"Device applying a load to measure true battery voltage under current draw â€” resting voltage is misleadingly high.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is thermal management for motors?", a:"Controlling heat buildup via software current limiting, lower duty cycle, heatsinks, or cooling fans.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"What is a Kraken X60?", a:"High-performance brushless FRC motor from WestCoast Products with TalonFX-compatible controller. 6,000 RPM, 9.37 NÂ·m stall torque.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a NEO 550?", a:"REV compact brushless FRC motor. 11,000 RPM free speed, 0.97 NÂ·m stall torque. Used for lower-load mechanisms like indexers.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is motor characterization (SysId)?", a:"WPILib tool measuring kS (static friction), kV (velocity constant), kA (acceleration constant) for accurate feedforward control.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is back-drivability related to motors?", a:"A motor with low gear reduction can be back-driven by external forces. High reductions (worm gears) hold position when unpowered.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is regenerative braking?", a:"When a motor decelerates, its back-EMF can be used to slow it down and return energy to the system.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is motor efficiency?", a:"Î· = P_mechanical / P_electrical = (Ï„ Ã— Ï‰) / (V Ã— I). Most efficient near maximum power point, not at stall.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a winding resistance?", a:"Internal resistance of motor coils. With V=12V and winding resistance R, stall current = V/R = 12/R amperes.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is motor speed control via PWM?", a:"Motor controllers vary average voltage to a motor by switching PWM on/off rapidly (typically 20kHz+). Higher duty cycle = more average voltage.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a brushless motor ESC?", a:"Electronic Speed Controller for brushless motors. Reads phase back-EMF to determine rotor position for commutation without a physical encoder.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a battery C-rating?", a:"Rate of discharge: 1C = full discharge in 1 hour. Higher C = can deliver more current without overheating.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW v6 ---
      { q:"What is voltage in the context of motors?", a:"Voltage drives current through the motor windings. Higher voltage = more current = more torque at the same resistance. FRC/FTC robots run on 12V nominal.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is motor direction control?", a:"Reversing the polarity of voltage applied to a brushed motor reverses its direction. Motor controllers do this electronically via an H-bridge circuit.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a gearbox?", a:"A set of gears reducing motor speed and increasing output torque. All FRC/FTC motors need gearboxes â€” motor shaft speeds (6000+ RPM) are too fast for direct drive.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What does 'free run' mean for a motor?", a:"The motor spinning without any load attached. At free run, current is minimal and speed is at its maximum. Real operating conditions fall between free run and stall.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a motor's no-load current?", a:"The small current drawn spinning freely with no load â€” overcomes bearing friction and back-EMF. Typically 1â€“3A. Much lower than stall current.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a battery capacity (Ah)?", a:"Amp-hours: how long a battery can deliver current. 18Ah at 1A = 18 hours. At 18A = 1 hour. FRC SLA batteries are ~18Ah. High-current robot use depletes them in minutes.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a motor driver IC?", a:"An integrated circuit like the DRV8833 that controls small brushed motors directly from a microcontroller. Used in custom electronics and small FTC mechanisms.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is back-EMF voltage sensing?", a:"Measuring the voltage a motor generates when it's spinning to estimate its speed without an encoder. Used in some simple speed-control circuits.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a motor's heat dissipation?", a:"Power lost to heat = IÂ²R (where R is winding resistance). At stall current, heating is extreme. Current limiting prevents thermal damage in sustained stall conditions.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a battery's state of charge (SOC)?", a:"The current charge level as a percentage (0â€“100%). Resting voltage gives a rough SOC estimate but load testing is more accurate for SLA batteries.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a brushless motor's pole count?", a:"Number of magnetic pole pairs. More poles = more torque ripple but smoother at low speed. Affects the electrical-to-mechanical speed ratio: mech RPM = elec RPM / pole pairs.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a motor's torque constant (kT)?", a:"Torque per amp: Ï„ = kT Ã— I. Related to kV by kT = 1/kV (in SI units). Higher kT = more torque per amp â€” useful for comparing motors of similar size.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a battery equalizer?", a:"A circuit balancing voltage between cells in a multi-cell battery pack â€” prevents weaker cells from over-discharging and degrading faster than the rest.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is pulse skipping in a motor controller?", a:"At very low duty cycles, controllers skip PWM pulses rather than using extremely short ones â€” maintains controllability at low speeds.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a Vortex motor?", a:"REV's second-generation FRC brushless motor (2023+) designed specifically for the SPARK Flex controller. Higher power density than the NEO in the same form factor.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is motor inductance?", a:"Resistance to changes in current flow. High inductance motors respond more slowly to controller commands but generate less electrical noise. Relevant for controller tuning.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a sinusoidal commutation?", a:"Driving motor phases with smooth sine waves instead of square waves â€” reduces torque ripple, runs quieter, and is more efficient. Used in field-oriented control (FOC).", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a Peukert effect?", a:"SLA battery capacity decreases at higher discharge rates. A 18Ah battery at 18A doesn't actually last 1 hour â€” it delivers less due to internal resistance heating.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a motor's operating point?", a:"The actual speed and torque at which a motor runs given its load and gear ratio. The operating point should fall near the maximum power point for efficiency.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is flux weakening in a BLDC motor?", a:"Injecting negative d-axis current to reduce the effective magnetic flux, allowing the motor to spin beyond its rated speed at reduced torque. Used in some FRC high-speed applications.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

  // â”€â”€â”€ 16. FUNDRAISING â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
  fundraising: {
    name: "Fundraising",
    icon: "ðŸ’°",
    color: "#16a34a",
    cards: [
      // BEGINNER
      { q:"Why do FIRST teams need to fundraise?", a:"Registration fees (~$5,000â€“$6,000 for FRC), parts, tools, travel, and competition costs add up to $15,000â€“$50,000+ per season.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a team sponsor?", a:"A business or organization providing money, materials, or services to the team in exchange for recognition (logo on robot, jersey, website).", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a team fundraiser?", a:"An event or campaign (bake sale, robotics camp, GoFundMe, car wash, raffle) to raise money from the broader community.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is in-kind sponsorship?", a:"A sponsor providing goods or services instead of cash â€” e.g., a machine shop donating parts, a company donating tools or computer equipment.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a donation letter?", a:"A written request for financial support sent to potential sponsors and community members. Should be concise, personal, and compelling.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is FIRST's grant program?", a:"FIRST offers Team Grants and assistance programs for teams demonstrating financial need. Apply early each season at firstinspires.org.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a 501(c)(3) and why does it matter for fundraising?", a:"Non-profit tax-exempt status. Donors can write off their donations on taxes, making your team much more attractive to corporate sponsors.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a team's elevator pitch?", a:"A 30-second summary of who you are, what FIRST is, and why someone should support you. Every team member should know it by heart.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a sponsorship packet?", a:"A professional document describing your team, mission, sponsor benefits (logo placement, recognition), and sponsorship tier options.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a robotics camp?", a:"A team-run multi-day camp teaching robotics/coding to younger students â€” earns revenue, builds outreach hours, and creates future team members.", level:"beginner" },
      // INTERMEDIATE
      { q:"What is a sponsorship tier structure?", a:"Categorized levels (Gold: $5k+, Silver: $2k, Bronze: $500) with different recognition benefits per tier â€” simplifies asks and stewardship.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a corporate matching program?", a:"Many companies match employee charitable donations dollar-for-dollar. Ask sponsors if their company has a matching program to double your funding.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a grant and how do you find them?", a:"A grant is non-repayable funding from a foundation, company, or government. Search tools: GrantWatch, Candid (Foundation Directory), FIRST's grant portal.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a STEM education grant?", a:"Grants specifically for K-12 STEM programs. Examples: Google.org, Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Home Depot Foundation, and local community foundations.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a stewardship plan?", a:"A plan for keeping sponsors engaged after they give: thank-you notes, progress updates, event invitations, and annual impact reports.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a team's value proposition?", a:"What a sponsor gets in return: logo exposure (robot at 50+ events), workforce pipeline (future employees), tax deduction, and community goodwill.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a crowdfunding campaign?", a:"Raising money online through platforms like GoFundMe, Kickstarter, or Donors Choose. Effective when shared widely on social media.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a community foundation grant?", a:"Local community foundations (e.g., your city's community foundation) often have open grant cycles for education and youth programs.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is alumni giving in FIRST?", a:"Former team members who go on to professional careers can become major donors and mentors. Maintain alumni relationships for long-term fundraising.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a walk-a-thon or pledge drive?", a:"Fundraiser where supporters pledge money per mile/step walked by team members â€” combines fitness, fun, and community engagement.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a silent auction?", a:"Fundraising event where donated items are displayed with bid sheets â€” attendees write bids anonymously and the highest bidder wins.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a school district funding request?", a:"Formally requesting funds from your school or district budget. Requires a written proposal, meeting with administrators, and board approval in some cases.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a team budget and why track it?", a:"A detailed income/expense plan. Tracking shows sponsors responsible use of their money and helps the team avoid shortfalls mid-season.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a thank-you note and when to send it?", a:"A written acknowledgment of a donation sent within 48 hours. Builds goodwill and significantly increases the likelihood of repeat giving.", level:"intermediate" },
      // ADVANCED
      { q:"What is a major donor strategy?", a:"Identifying and cultivating relationships with individuals or companies capable of $5,000+ gifts. Requires personalized outreach and relationship building.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a multi-year sponsorship agreement?", a:"A formal agreement where a sponsor commits to funding for 2â€“3 years in exchange for guaranteed recognition and partnership benefits.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a case for support?", a:"A comprehensive document telling your team's story, demonstrating impact, and making a compelling argument for why someone should invest in your mission.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is prospect research?", a:"Researching potential sponsors to understand their giving history, capacity, and interests before making an ask â€” improves targeting and personalization.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a naming opportunity?", a:"Offering a prominent sponsorship recognition in exchange for a large gift: 'The [Company] Drive Team', logo on a prominent robot component, etc.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is an endowment?", a:"A permanently invested fund where only the interest/earnings are spent. An endowed team fund provides stable long-term income regardless of annual fundraising.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is an impact report for funders?", a:"An annual document sent to all donors showing exactly how their money was used and what results were achieved â€” critical for donor retention.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a grant reporting requirement?", a:"Many grants require you to submit a report after the grant period documenting how funds were spent and outcomes achieved. Missing reports may disqualify future grants.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a fundraising goal and how do you set it?", a:"Calculate total season expenses (registration, parts, travel, tools) then subtract confirmed income. The gap is your fundraising goal. Set stretch goals 10â€“15% above.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a title sponsor?", a:"A premier sponsorship level where a company gets maximum branding â€” often their name incorporated into the team's public identity for the season.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a letter of inquiry (LOI)?", a:"A brief 1â€“2 page letter sent to foundations before a full grant application. Describes your team and project â€” foundations invite a full proposal if interested.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a diversified funding strategy?", a:"Spreading revenue across many sources (corporate sponsors, grants, crowdfunding, events, school funding) so losing one source doesn't devastate the team.", level:"advanced" },
      // --- NEW v6 ---
      { q:"What is a bake sale?", a:"A classic team fundraiser where members sell homemade goods. Low overhead, builds community goodwill, and can raise $200â€“$500 at a single event.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a car wash fundraiser?", a:"Team members wash cars in a public parking lot for donations. Requires supplies (~$50) and can raise $500â€“$1,500 in a single day.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a team's fiscal year?", a:"The 12-month accounting period for tracking income and expenses. Many school-based teams follow the academic year (Septâ€“Aug) for their fiscal year.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a tax receipt for donors?", a:"A written acknowledgment of a tax-deductible donation including donor name, amount, date, and your team's EIN/tax ID. Required for donors claiming a deduction.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is an EIN?", a:"Employer Identification Number â€” a federal tax ID assigned by the IRS. Required to open a bank account, receive grant funding, and issue tax receipts for donations.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a team PayPal or Square account?", a:"A digital payment account allowing the team to accept card payments at fundraising events and online donations. Essential for modern fundraising.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a fundraising goal thermometer?", a:"A visual tracker showing progress toward a fundraising goal. Posted publicly (social media, school hallway) it creates accountability and motivates donors to push you to 100%.", level:"beginner" },
      { q:"What is a silent auction item procurement?", a:"Contacting local businesses to donate items or experiences (gift cards, sports tickets, restaurant meals) for a silent auction â€” most items are donated at no cost.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a 'friend of the team' individual donor?", a:"A community member (parent, alumni, neighbor) making a personal donation. Small individual gifts ($25â€“$100) add up â€” cultivate these relationships year-round.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is an online fundraising page?", a:"A dedicated page on GoFundMe, Givebutter, or DonorBox with your team's story, photos, and goal â€” shareable via social media and email for broad reach.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a gala or dinner fundraiser?", a:"A formal fundraising event with speakers, a meal, and a live or silent auction. High revenue potential ($5,000â€“$50,000+) but requires significant planning.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a read-a-thon or STEM-a-thon?", a:"Students collect pledges for completing a challenge (reading hours, coding problems solved, robot tasks completed). Engages parents as donors while showcasing skills.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a memorial or tribute fund?", a:"A special fund accepting gifts in honor of someone. Families sometimes establish tribute funds when a beloved mentor or community member passes away.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a planned giving ask?", a:"Asking supporters to include the team/nonprofit in their will or estate plan. Long-term strategy â€” not appropriate for student-run teams but relevant for incorporated foundations.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a pay-to-play fee?", a:"Some teams charge members an annual participation fee ($50â€“$500) to offset costs while keeping the program accessible. Must be applied with scholarship options for equity.", level:"intermediate" },
      { q:"What is a fundraising committee?", a:"A dedicated subteam of students and parents focused exclusively on identifying sponsors, running campaigns, and stewarding donors â€” separates fundraising from build season pressure.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is donor segmentation?", a:"Grouping donors by giving level, history, and interests to tailor communication â€” major donors get personal calls; small donors get newsletters. Improves retention rates.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a capital campaign?", a:"A major fundraising drive for a specific large-scale need (new shop space, CNC machine, van). Set a specific goal, timeline, and list of lead donors before going public.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a giving day?", a:"A 24-hour online fundraising event (like Giving Tuesday) where donors give online. Some community foundations offer matching funds, making giving days very high-leverage.", level:"advanced" },
      { q:"What is a corporate volunteer grant?", a:"Many companies give grants to nonprofits where their employees volunteer. If a mentor's employer has this program, their volunteer hours at your team can generate cash grants.", level:"advanced" },
    ]
  },

};

// â”€â”€â”€ FLASHCARD PAGE â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
function FlashcardsPage({ user }) {
  const [deck, setDeck] = useState(null);
  const [cardIdx, setCardIdx] = useState(0);
  const [flipped, setFlipped] = useState(false);
  const [ratings, setRatings] = useState({});
  const [shuffled, setShuffled] = useState([]);
  const [sessionDone, setSessionDone] = useState(false);
  const [progress, setProgress] = useState({});
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
  const [levelFilter, setLevelFilter] = useState("all");

  useEffect(()=>{
    if (user) storeGet("hub-flashcards-"+user.username, false).then(d=>{ if(d) setProgress(typeof d==="object"?d:{}); });
  },[user]);

  function startDeck(deckId, lvl) {
    const allCards = FLASHCARD_DECKS[deckId].cards;
    const filtered = (lvl && lvl !== "all") ? allCards.filter(c => c.level === lvl) : allCards;
    const cards = filtered.length > 0 ? filtered : allCards;
    // Map filtered cards back to original indices for progress tracking
    const cardIndices = cards.map(c => allCards.indexOf(c));
    const saved = progress[deckId] || {};
    const unknowns = cardIndices.filter(i=>saved[i]!=="know");
    const order = shuffleArr(unknowns.length>0?unknowns:cardIndices);
    setDeck(deckId); setShuffled(order.length?order:cardIndices);
    setCardIdx(0); setFlipped(false); setRatings({}); setSessionDone(false);
  }

  async function rateCard(rating) {
    const realIdx = shuffled[cardIdx];
    const nr = {...ratings, [realIdx]: rating};
    setRatings(nr);
    const newProg = {...(progress[deck]||{})};
    if (rating==="know") newProg[realIdx]="know";
    else delete newProg[realIdx];
    const newAllProg = {...progress, [deck]: newProg};
    setProgress(newAllProg);
    if (user) await storeSet("hub-flashcards-"+user.username, newAllProg, false);
    if (cardIdx+1 >= shuffled.length) setSessionDone(true);
    else { setCardIdx(cardIdx+1); setFlipped(false); }
  }

  function restart() { startDeck(deck); }
  function backToDecks() { setDeck(null); setSessionDone(false); }

  const deckKeys = Object.keys(FLASHCARD_DECKS);
  const totalCards = deck ? FLASHCARD_DECKS[deck].cards.length : 0;
  const knownCount = deck ? Object.values(progress[deck]||{}).filter(v=>v==="know").length : 0;

  if (!deck) {
    return (
      <div style={{maxWidth:800,margin:"0 auto",padding:"24px 16px"}}>
        <div style={{marginBottom:16}}>
          <div style={{fontWeight:900,fontSize:24,color:"#1e293b",marginBottom:6}}>ðŸƒ Flashcard Decks</div>
          <div style={{color:"#64748b",fontSize:14,marginBottom:12}}>Memorize key concepts with spaced repetition. Cards you mark "Still Learning" come back more often.</div>
          <div style={{display:"flex",gap:8,flexWrap:"wrap",alignItems:"center"}}>
            <span style={{fontSize:12,color:"#94a3b8",fontWeight:600}}>Filter by level:</span>
            {["all","beginner","intermediate","advanced"].map(lvl=>(
              <button key={lvl} onClick={()=>setLevelFilter(lvl)}
                style={{background:levelFilter===lvl?(lvl==="all"?"#1d4ed8":lvl==="beginner"?"#16a34a":lvl==="intermediate"?"#d97706":"#7c3aed"):"#f1f5f9",color:levelFilter===lvl?"#fff":"#374151",border:"none",borderRadius:20,padding:"4px 14px",cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:12,fontFamily:"inherit",textTransform:"capitalize"}}>
                {lvl==="all"?"All Levels":lvl}
              </button>
            ))}
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style={{display:"grid",gridTemplateColumns:"repeat(auto-fill,minmax(240px,1fr))",gap:16}}>
          {deckKeys.map(dk=>{
            const d = FLASHCARD_DECKS[dk];
            const total = d.cards.length;
            const known = Object.values(progress[dk]||{}).filter(v=>v==="know").length;
            const pct = Math.round(known/total*100);
            return (
              <div key={dk} onClick={()=>startDeck(dk,levelFilter)} style={{background:"#fff",borderRadius:16,padding:22,border:"1px solid #e2e8f0",cursor:"pointer",transition:"all 0.2s",boxShadow:"0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.04)"}}
                onMouseEnter={e=>{e.currentTarget.style.transform="translateY(-3px)";e.currentTarget.style.boxShadow="0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)";}}
                onMouseLeave={e=>{e.currentTarget.style.transform="none";e.currentTarget.style.boxShadow="0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.04)";}}>
                <div style={{fontSize:32,marginBottom:10}}>{d.icon}</div>
                <div style={{fontWeight:800,fontSize:16,color:"#1e293b",marginBottom:4}}>{d.name}</div>
                <div style={{fontSize:13,color:"#64748b",marginBottom:8}}>
                  {total} cards total
                  {levelFilter!=="all" && <span style={{marginLeft:8,background:levelFilter==="beginner"?"#dcfce7":levelFilter==="intermediate"?"#fef9c3":"#ede9fe",color:levelFilter==="beginner"?"#15803d":levelFilter==="intermediate"?"#854d0e":"#6d28d9",fontSize:11,fontWeight:700,padding:"1px 8px",borderRadius:999}}>{d.cards.filter(c=>c.level===levelFilter).length} {levelFilter}</span>}
                </div>
                <div style={{background:"#f1f5f9",borderRadius:999,height:6,marginBottom:6}}>
                  <div style={{width:(pct) + "%",background:d.color,height:"100%",borderRadius:999,transition:"width 0.4s"}}></div>
                </div>
                <div style={{fontSize:12,color:"#94a3b8"}}>{known}/{total} mastered ({pct}%)</div>
              </div>
            );
          })}
        </div>
      </div>
    );
  }

  const d = FLASHCARD_DECKS[deck];
  const card = d.cards[shuffled[cardIdx]];

  if (sessionDone) {
    const knew = Object.values(ratings).filter(r=>r==="know").length;
    const studying = Object.values(ratings).filter(r=>r==="study").length;
    return (
      <div style={{maxWidth:600,margin:"40px auto",padding:"0 16px",textAlign:"center"}}>
        <div style={{background:"#fff",borderRadius:20,padding:"36px 32px",boxShadow:"0 4px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)"}}>
          <div style={{fontSize:52,marginBottom:16}}>ðŸŽ‰</div>
          <div style={{fontWeight:900,fontSize:22,marginBottom:8}}>Session Complete!</div>
          <div style={{color:"#64748b",marginBottom:24}}>You reviewed {shuffled.length} cards from <strong>{d.name}</strong></div>
          <div style={{display:"flex",gap:12,justifyContent:"center",marginBottom:28}}>
            <div style={{background:"#f0fdf4",borderRadius:12,padding:"16px 22px",minWidth:100}}>
              <div style={{fontSize:24,fontWeight:800,color:"#10b981"}}>{knew}</div>
              <div style={{fontSize:12,color:"#64748b"}}>Got it âœ“</div>
            </div>
            <div style={{background:"#fffbeb",borderRadius:12,padding:"16px 22px",minWidth:100}}>
              <div style={{fontSize:24,fontWeight:800,color:"#f59e0b"}}>{studying}</div>
              <div style={{fontSize:12,color:"#64748b"}}>Still learning</div>
            </div>
            <div style={{background:"#eff6ff",borderRadius:12,padding:"16px 22px",minWidth:100}}>
              <div style={{fontSize:24,fontWeight:800,color:"#1d4ed8"}}>{knownCount}/{totalCards}</div>
              <div style={{fontSize:12,color:"#64748b"}}>Total mastered</div>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div style={{display:"flex",gap:10,justifyContent:"center"}}>
            {studying>0&&<button onClick={restart} style={{background:"#1d4ed8",color:"#fff",border:"none",borderRadius:10,padding:"12px 24px",cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700}}>Review Missed Cards</button>}
            <button onClick={restart} style={{background:"#f1f5f9",color:"#475569",border:"none",borderRadius:10,padding:"12px 24px",cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:600}}>Full Shuffle Again</button>
            <button onClick={backToDecks} style={{background:"none",color:"#64748b",border:"1px solid #e2e8f0",borderRadius:10,padding:"12px 24px",cursor:"pointer"}}>Back to Decks</button>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    );
  }

  return (
    <div style={{maxWidth:640,margin:"0 auto",padding:"24px 16px"}}>
      <div style={{display:"flex",alignItems:"center",gap:12,marginBottom:20}}>
        <button onClick={backToDecks} style={{background:"none",border:"none",cursor:"pointer",fontSize:13,color:"#64748b",padding:0}}>â† All Decks</button>
        <div style={{fontWeight:800,fontSize:16,color:"#1e293b"}}>{d.icon} {d.name}</div>
        <div style={{marginLeft:"auto",fontSize:13,color:"#94a3b8"}}>{cardIdx+1} / {shuffled.length}</div>
      </div>

      {/* Progress bar */}
      <div style={{background:"#e2e8f0",borderRadius:999,height:5,marginBottom:20}}>
        <div style={{width:(((cardIdx)/shuffled.length)*100) + "%",background:d.color,height:"100%",borderRadius:999,transition:"width 0.3s"}}></div>
      </div>

      {/* Flashcard */}
      <div onClick={()=>setFlipped(!flipped)} style={{
        cursor:"pointer",perspective:1200,marginBottom:20,userSelect:"none"
      }}>
        <div style={{
          position:"relative",minHeight:220,
          transformStyle:"preserve-3d",
          transform:flipped?"rotateY(180deg)":"rotateY(0deg)",
          transition:"transform 0.4s ease"
        }}>
          {/* Front */}
          <div style={{position:"absolute",inset:0,backfaceVisibility:"hidden",
            background:"#fff",borderRadius:20,padding:"32px 28px",display:"flex",flexDirection:"column",
            alignItems:"center",justifyContent:"center",textAlign:"center",
            boxShadow:"0 4px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)",border:"2px solid " + (d.color) + "20"}}>
            <div style={{fontSize:11,fontWeight:700,color:d.color,textTransform:"uppercase",letterSpacing:1,marginBottom:16}}>â“ Question</div>
            {card?.level && <div style={{background:card.level==="beginner"?"#dcfce7":card.level==="intermediate"?"#fef9c3":"#ede9fe",color:card.level==="beginner"?"#15803d":card.level==="intermediate"?"#854d0e":"#6d28d9",fontSize:10,fontWeight:700,padding:"2px 10px",borderRadius:999,marginBottom:10,display:"inline-block",textTransform:"capitalize"}}>{card.level}</div>}
            <div style={{fontWeight:700,fontSize:18,color:"#1e293b",lineHeight:1.5}}>{card?.q}</div>
            <div style={{position:"absolute",bottom:16,right:20,fontSize:11,color:"#94a3b8"}}>Tap to flip</div>
          </div>
          {/* Back */}
          <div style={{position:"absolute",inset:0,backfaceVisibility:"hidden",
            transform:"rotateY(180deg)",
            background:d.color,borderRadius:20,padding:"32px 28px",display:"flex",flexDirection:"column",
            alignItems:"center",justifyContent:"center",textAlign:"center",
            boxShadow:"0 4px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)"}}>
            <div style={{fontSize:11,fontWeight:700,color:"rgba(255,255,255,0.7)",textTransform:"uppercase",letterSpacing:1,marginBottom:16}}>ðŸ’¡ Answer</div>
            <div style={{fontWeight:600,fontSize:15,color:"#fff",lineHeight:1.7}}>{card?.a}</div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      {flipped && (
        <div style={{display:"flex",gap:12,justifyContent:"center"}}>
          <button onClick={()=>rateCard("study")} style={{flex:1,background:"#fff",color:"#f59e0b",border:"2px solid #fde68a",borderRadius:12,padding:"14px 20px",cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:15,transition:"all 0.15s"}}
            onMouseEnter={e=>e.currentTarget.style.background="#fffbeb"}
            onMouseLeave={e=>e.currentTarget.style.background="#fff"}>
            ðŸ”„ Still Learning
          </button>
          <button onClick={()=>rateCard("know")} style={{flex:1,background:"#10b981",color:"#fff",border:"2px solid #10b981",borderRadius:12,padding:"14px 20px",cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:15,transition:"all 0.15s"}}
            onMouseEnter={e=>e.currentTarget.style.background="#059669"}
            onMouseLeave={e=>e.currentTarget.style.background="#10b981"}>
            âœ“ Got It!
          </button>
        </div>
      )}
      {!flipped && (
        <div style={{textAlign:"center",color:"#94a3b8",fontSize:13,marginTop:8}}>ðŸ‘† Tap the card to reveal the answer</div>
      )}

      {/* Mini mastery stats */}
      <div style={{marginTop:20,background:"#f8fafc",borderRadius:12,padding:"12px 16px",display:"flex",gap:16,justifyContent:"center",fontSize:12,color:"#64748b"}}>
        <span>ðŸ† Mastered: <strong>{knownCount}/{totalCards}</strong></span>
        <span>ðŸ“‹ This session: <strong>{cardIdx}/{shuffled.length}</strong></span>
        <span style={{color:"#10b981"}}>âœ“ {Object.values(ratings).filter(r=>r==="know").length} got it</span>
        <span style={{color:"#f59e0b"}}>ðŸ”„ {Object.values(ratings).filter(r=>r==="study").length} reviewing</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

// â”€â”€â”€ STUDENT PROGRESS REPORT â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
// Helper: syntax-highlight a Java/JS code line (called outside JSX to avoid </g parser issue)
function highlightJava(line) {
  const lt = '\x3c', gt = '\x3e';
  return line
    .replace(/&/g,"&amp;").replace(/\x3c/g,"&lt;").replace(/\x3e/g,"&gt;")
    .replace(/(\/\/[^\n]*)/g,'<span style="color:#64748b">$1</span>')
    .replace(/\b(if|else|while|for|return|void|int|double|boolean|String|new|class|public|private|static)\b/g,'<span style="color:#c084fc">$1</span>')
    .replace(/\b(true|false|null)\b/g,'<span style="color:#fb923c">$1</span>')
    .replace(/"([^"]*)"/g,'<span style="color:#86efac">&quot;$1&quot;</span>')
    .replace(/\b(\d+\.?\d*)\b/g,'<span style="color:#f9a8d4">$1</span>');
}

function BlocksLesson({ lesson }) {
  const [step, setStep] = useState(0);
  const [assembled, setAssembled] = useState([]);
  const [phase, setPhase] = useState("learn"); // learn | build | quiz | done
  const [quizIdx, setQuizIdx] = useState(0);
  const [quizAns, setQuizAns] = useState(null);
  const [quizScore, setQuizScore] = useState(0);

  const BLOCK_COLORS = {
    control:    {bg:"#fef3c7", border:"#f59e0b", text:"#92400e", icon:"ðŸ”„"},
    action:     {bg:"#dbeafe", border:"#3b82f6", text:"#1e40af", icon:"âš¡"},
    sensor:     {bg:"#d1fae5", border:"#10b981", text:"#065f46", icon:"ðŸ“¡"},
    variable:   {bg:"#ede9fe", border:"#8b5cf6", text:"#4c1d95", icon:"ðŸ“¦"},
    comment:    {bg:"#f1f5f9", border:"#94a3b8", text:"#475569", icon:"ðŸ’¬"},
    math:       {bg:"#fce7f3", border:"#ec4899", text:"#9d174d", icon:"âž•"},
  };

  const blocks = lesson.blocks || [];
  const quizzes = lesson.quiz || [];
  const currentBlock = blocks[step];

  if (phase === "learn") return (
    <div>
      <div style={{background:"linear-gradient(135deg,#7c3aed,#4f46e5)",borderRadius:14,padding:20,color:"#fff",marginBottom:18}}>
        <div style={{fontSize:26,marginBottom:6}}>ðŸ§© Block Programming</div>
        <div style={{fontSize:14,opacity:0.9,lineHeight:1.6}}>{lesson.intro || "Learn Java concepts through visual blocks â€” then write the real code."}</div>
        <div style={{fontSize:12,opacity:0.7,marginTop:8}}>{blocks.length} code blocks Â· Visual + Text learning</div>
      </div>
      {blocks.map((block, i) => {
        const c = BLOCK_COLORS[block.type] || BLOCK_COLORS.action;
        const isVisible = i <= step;
        return (
          <div key={i} style={{marginBottom:12,opacity:isVisible?1:0.35,transition:"opacity 0.3s"}}>
            {/* Block header */}
            <div style={{display:"flex",alignItems:"stretch",borderRadius:10,overflow:"hidden",border:"2px solid " + (c.border),boxShadow:"0 2px 8px " + (c.border) + "30"}}>
              {/* Left notch connector */}
              <div style={{width:14,background:c.border,flexShrink:0,position:"relative"}}>
                {i>0 && <div style={{position:"absolute",top:-2,left:"50%",transform:"translateX(-50%)",width:10,height:10,borderRadius:"50%",background:"#fff",border:"2px solid " + (c.border)}}/>}
                {i<blocks.length-1 && <div style={{position:"absolute",bottom:-2,left:"50%",transform:"translateX(-50%)",width:10,height:10,borderRadius:"50%",background:"#fff",border:"2px solid " + (c.border)}}/>}
              </div>
              <div style={{flex:1,background:c.bg,padding:"12px 16px"}}>
                <div style={{display:"flex",alignItems:"center",gap:8,marginBottom:8}}>
                  <span style={{fontSize:18}}>{c.icon}</span>
                  <span style={{fontSize:11,fontWeight:800,textTransform:"uppercase",letterSpacing:1,color:c.text,background:c.border+"25",padding:"2px 8px",borderRadius:20}}>{block.type}</span>
                  <span style={{fontWeight:800,fontSize:14,color:c.text,marginLeft:4}}>{block.label}</span>
                </div>
                {/* Visual block body */}
                <div style={{background:"#0f172a",borderRadius:8,padding:"10px 14px",marginBottom:10,fontFamily:"'Fira Code','Courier New',monospace",fontSize:13,color:"#e2e8f0",lineHeight:1.7,border:"1px solid " + (c.border) + "40"}}>
                  {block.code.split('\n').map((line, li) => (
                    <div key={li} style={{display:"flex"}}>
                      <span style={{color:"#475569",fontSize:11,minWidth:24,userSelect:"none",marginRight:8}}>{li+1}</span>
                      <span dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: highlightJava(line)}}/>
                    </div>
                  ))}
                </div>
                <div style={{fontSize:13,color:c.text,lineHeight:1.6,background:"#fff8",borderRadius:7,padding:"8px 12px"}}>{block.explanation}</div>
              </div>
            </div>
            {/* Bottom connector line */}
            {i < blocks.length-1 && (
              <div style={{display:"flex",justifyContent:"center"}}>
                <div style={{width:2,height:16,background:isVisible?c.border:"#e2e8f0",transition:"background 0.3s"}}/>
              </div>
            )}
          </div>
        );
      })}
      <div style={{display:"flex",gap:10,marginTop:16,flexWrap:"wrap"}}>
        {step < blocks.length-1 && (
          <button onClick={()=>setStep(s=>s+1)} style={{background:"#7c3aed",color:"#fff",border:"none",padding:"11px 24px",borderRadius:9,cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:14,fontFamily:"inherit"}}>
            Next Block â†’
          </button>
        )}
        {step >= blocks.length-1 && (
          <button onClick={()=>{setPhase("quiz");setQuizIdx(0);setQuizAns(null);}} style={{background:"#059669",color:"#fff",border:"none",padding:"11px 24px",borderRadius:9,cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:14,fontFamily:"inherit"}}>
            Take Quiz âœ“
          </button>
        )}
        {step > 0 && <button onClick={()=>setStep(s=>s-1)} style={{background:"#f1f5f9",color:"#374151",border:"none",padding:"11px 18px",borderRadius:9,cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:14,fontFamily:"inherit"}}>â† Back</button>}
      </div>
    </div>
  );

  if (phase === "quiz" && quizzes.length > 0) {
    const q = quizzes[quizIdx];
    const answered = quizAns !== null;
    return (
      <div>
        <div style={{display:"flex",justifyContent:"space-between",alignItems:"center",marginBottom:16}}>
          <div style={{fontWeight:800,fontSize:15}}>ðŸ§© Blocks Quiz â€” Question {quizIdx+1}/{quizzes.length}</div>
          <div style={{fontSize:13,color:"#7c3aed",fontWeight:700}}>Score: {quizScore}/{quizIdx}</div>
        </div>
        <div style={{background:"#f8f4ff",border:"2px solid #c4b5fd",borderRadius:12,padding:16,marginBottom:16}}>
          <div style={{fontWeight:700,fontSize:15,color:"#4c1d95",lineHeight:1.6}}>{q.q}</div>
          {q.code && (
            <div style={{background:"#0f172a",borderRadius:8,padding:"10px 14px",marginTop:10,fontFamily:"monospace",fontSize:13,color:"#e2e8f0"}}>{q.code}</div>
          )}
        </div>
        <div style={{display:"flex",flexDirection:"column",gap:8,marginBottom:16}}>
          {q.opts.map((opt,j) => {
            let bg="#f8fafc",border="1.5px solid #e2e8f0",col="#374151";
            if(answered){
              if(j===q.ans){bg="#f0fdf4";border="2px solid #86efac";col="#166534";}
              else if(quizAns===j){bg="#fef2f2";border="2px solid #fca5a5";col="#991b1b";}
            } else if(quizAns===j){bg="#f3e8ff";border="2px solid #c084fc";col="#7c3aed";}
            return (
              <button key={j} onClick={()=>{if(!answered){setQuizAns(j);if(j===q.ans)setQuizScore(s=>s+1);}}}
                style={{background:bg,border,color:col,padding:"11px 16px",borderRadius:10,cursor:answered?"default":"pointer",textAlign:"left",fontWeight:600,fontSize:14,fontFamily:"inherit"}}>
                {["A","B","C","D"][j]}. {opt}
              </button>
            );
          })}
        </div>
        {answered && (
          <div style={{background:"#f3e8ff",border:"2px solid #c4b5fd",borderRadius:10,padding:12,marginBottom:14,fontSize:13,color:"#4c1d95",lineHeight:1.6}}>
            {q.explanation || (quizAns===q.ans ? "âœ… Correct!" : "ðŸ’¡ The answer is " + (["A","B","C","D"][q.ans]) + ".")}
          </div>
        )}
        {answered && (
          <button onClick={()=>{
            if(quizIdx+1 >= quizzes.length){setPhase("done");}
            else{setQuizIdx(i=>i+1);setQuizAns(null);}
          }} style={{background:"#7c3aed",color:"#fff",border:"none",padding:"11px 24px",borderRadius:9,cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:14,fontFamily:"inherit"}}>
            {quizIdx+1>=quizzes.length?"Finish âœ“":"Next Question â†’"}
          </button>
        )}
      </div>
    );
  }

  return (
    <div style={{background:"linear-gradient(135deg,#4c1d95,#7c3aed)",borderRadius:14,padding:24,color:"#fff",textAlign:"center"}}>
      <div style={{fontSize:48,marginBottom:10}}>ðŸ§©</div>
      <div style={{fontSize:22,fontWeight:900,marginBottom:6}}>Blocks Complete!</div>
      <div style={{fontSize:15,opacity:0.85,marginBottom:6}}>Quiz score: {quizScore}/{quizzes.length}</div>
      <div style={{fontSize:13,opacity:0.7,marginBottom:18}}>You've learned {blocks.length} code blocks with explanations.</div>
      <button onClick={()=>{setPhase("learn");setStep(0);setQuizIdx(0);setQuizAns(null);setQuizScore(0);}}
        style={{background:"rgba(255,255,255,0.2)",border:"2px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.5)",color:"#fff",padding:"9px 22px",borderRadius:8,cursor:"pointer",fontWeight:700,fontSize:13,fontFamily:"inherit"}}>
        Review Blocks
      </button>
    </div>
  );
}

// â”€â”€â”€ STUDENT PROGRESS REPORT â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
function StudentReportPage({ user, done, totalLessons }) {
  const [quizScores, setQuizScores] = useState({});
  const [flashProg, setFlashProg] = useState({});
  const [learningTime, setLearningTime] = useState(0);
  const [streak, setStreak] = useState(0);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);

  useEffect(()=>{
    async function load() {
      const userData = await storeGet("hub-users", true);
      const u = userData?.[user.username] || {};
      setQuizScores(u.quizScores || {});
      setLearningTime(u.learningTime || 0);
      setStreak(u.streak || 0);
      const fp = await storeGet("hub-flashcards-"+user.username, false);
      setFlashProg(fp || {});
      setLoading(false);
    }
    load();
  }, [user, done]);

  if (loading) return <div style={{padding:40,textAlign:"center",color:"#64748b"}}>Loading your reportâ€¦</div>;

  // Per-subject stats
  const subjectStats = SUBJECTS.map(sub => {
    const subLessons = Object.values(LESSONS).flatMap(lvlObj => 
      (lvlObj[sub.id] || []).flatMap(lvl => 
        typeof lvl === "object" && !Array.isArray(lvl) ? [] : 
        (lvlObj[sub.id] || [])
      )
    );
    
    // Simpler: count done lessons by subject prefix
    // Get all lesson IDs for this subject directly from LESSONS
    const subjectLessons = Object.values(LESSONS[sub.id]||{}).flat();
    const subjectLessonIds = new Set(subjectLessons.map(l => l.id));
    const allIds = Object.keys(done);
    const doneSub = allIds.filter(id => subjectLessonIds.has(id));
    
    // Count total lessons for this subject
    const allLessonsFlat = Object.values(LESSONS).reduce((acc, lvlMap) => {
      const subArr = lvlMap[sub.id];
      if (Array.isArray(subArr)) subArr.forEach(l => acc.push(l.id));
      return acc;
    }, []);
    const total = Math.max(allLessonsFlat.length, 1);
    
    // Quiz scores for this subject
    const subQuizzes = Object.entries(quizScores).filter(([k]) => k.startsWith(sub.id));
    const avgQuiz = subQuizzes.length > 0
      ? Math.round(subQuizzes.reduce((s,[,v])=>s+(v.score/v.total*100),0)/subQuizzes.length)
      : null;

    const flashDeck = FLASHCARD_DECKS[sub.id];
    const flashKnown = flashDeck ? Object.values(flashProg[sub.id]||{}).filter(v=>v==="know").length : 0;
    const flashTotal = flashDeck ? flashDeck.cards.length : 0;

    return {
      ...sub,
      done: doneSub.length,
      total,
      pct: Math.round(doneSub.length/total*100),
      avgQuiz,
      flashKnown,
      flashTotal,
    };
  });

  const overallPct = Math.round(Object.keys(done).length / Math.max(totalLessons,1) * 100);
  const strengths = subjectStats.filter(s => s.pct >= 60 || (s.avgQuiz !== null && s.avgQuiz >= 75));
  const improve = subjectStats.filter(s => s.done > 0 && s.pct < 40 && (s.avgQuiz === null || s.avgQuiz < 60));
  const notStarted = subjectStats.filter(s => s.done === 0);

  // Recommended next lessons (incomplete, in subjects with some progress)
  const inProgress = subjectStats.filter(s => s.done > 0 && s.pct < 100);
  
  // Grade based on overall quiz average
  const allQuizArr = Object.values(quizScores);
  const overallQuizAvg = allQuizArr.length > 0
    ? Math.round(allQuizArr.reduce((s,v)=>s+(v.score/v.total*100),0)/allQuizArr.length) : null;
  const grade = overallQuizAvg === null ? "â€”" : overallQuizAvg >= 90 ? "A" : overallQuizAvg >= 80 ? "B" : overallQuizAvg >= 70 ? "C" : overallQuizAvg >= 60 ? "D" : "F";

  return (
    <div style={{maxWidth:900,margin:"0 auto",padding:"24px 16px"}}>
      {/* Header */}
      <div style={{background:"linear-gradient(135deg,#1e3a8a,#1d4ed8,#7c3aed)",borderRadius:20,padding:"28px 28px",color:"#fff",marginBottom:24,position:"relative",overflow:"hidden"}}>
        <div style={{position:"absolute",right:-20,top:-20,fontSize:120,opacity:0.05}}>ðŸ“Š</div>
        <div style={{fontSize:22,fontWeight:900,marginBottom:4}}>ðŸ“Š Your Learning Report</div>
        <div style={{opacity:0.8,marginBottom:18}}>Personalized analysis for {user.name || user.username}</div>
        <div style={{display:"flex",gap:20,flexWrap:"wrap"}}>
          {[
            {label:"Lessons Done",val:(Object.keys(done).length) + "/" + (totalLessons),icon:"ðŸ“š"},
            {label:"Overall Progress",val:(overallPct) + "%",icon:"ðŸ“ˆ"},
            {label:"Quiz Grade",val:grade,icon:"ðŸ§ "},
            {label:"Learning Time",val:fmtTime(learningTime),icon:"â±"},
            {label:"Day Streak",val:(streak) + "ðŸ”¥",icon:""},
            {label:"Quizzes Taken",val:allQuizArr.length,icon:"âœ…"},
          ].map(stat=>(
            <div key={stat.label} style={{background:"rgba(255,255,255,0.12)",borderRadius:12,padding:"12px 18px",minWidth:100}}>
              <div style={{fontSize:20,fontWeight:900}}>{stat.icon} {stat.val}</div>
              <div style={{fontSize:11,opacity:0.7,marginTop:2}}>{stat.label}</div>
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>
      </div>

      <div style={{display:"grid",gridTemplateColumns:"1fr 1fr",gap:16,marginBottom:20}}>
        {/* Subject breakdown */}
        <div style={{background:"#fff",borderRadius:16,padding:20,boxShadow:"0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.06)",gridColumn:"1/-1"}}>
          <div style={{fontWeight:800,fontSize:16,marginBottom:16}}>ðŸ“š Subject Progress Breakdown</div>
          {subjectStats.map(s=>(
            <div key={s.id} style={{marginBottom:14}}>
              <div style={{display:"flex",justifyContent:"space-between",alignItems:"center",marginBottom:5}}>
                <span style={{fontWeight:600,fontSize:14}}>{s.icon} {s.name}</span>
                <div style={{display:"flex",gap:12,alignItems:"center",fontSize:12,color:"#64748b"}}>
                  {s.avgQuiz!==null&&<span style={{background:s.avgQuiz>=80?"#f0fdf4":s.avgQuiz>=60?"#fffbeb":"#fef2f2",color:s.avgQuiz>=80?"#065f46":s.avgQuiz>=60?"#92400e":"#991b1b",padding:"2px 8px",borderRadius:6,fontWeight:700}}>Quiz: {s.avgQuiz}%</span>}
                  {s.flashTotal>0&&<span>ðŸƒ {s.flashKnown}/{s.flashTotal}</span>}
                  <span style={{fontWeight:700,color:s.pct>=60?"#10b981":s.pct>=30?"#f59e0b":"#ef4444"}}>{s.done}/{s.total} ({s.pct}%)</span>
                </div>
              </div>
              <div style={{background:"#f1f5f9",borderRadius:999,height:8}}>
                <div style={{width:(s.pct) + "%",background:s.color,height:"100%",borderRadius:999,transition:"width 0.5s"}}></div>
              </div>
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>

        {/* Strengths */}
        <div style={{background:"#f0fdf4",borderRadius:16,padding:20,border:"1px solid #bbf7d0"}}>
          <div style={{fontWeight:800,fontSize:15,color:"#065f46",marginBottom:12}}>ðŸ’ª Your Strengths</div>
          {strengths.length === 0 ? (
            <div style={{color:"#6b7280",fontSize:13}}>Complete more lessons and quizzes to identify your strengths.</div>
          ) : strengths.map(s=>(
            <div key={s.id} style={{display:"flex",alignItems:"center",gap:8,marginBottom:8,fontSize:13}}>
              <span>{s.icon}</span>
              <span style={{fontWeight:600,color:"#065f46"}}>{s.name}</span>
              {s.avgQuiz&&<span style={{marginLeft:"auto",background:"#10b981",color:"#fff",padding:"2px 8px",borderRadius:6,fontSize:11,fontWeight:700}}>{s.avgQuiz}% avg</span>}
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>

        {/* Areas to improve */}
        <div style={{background:"#fffbeb",borderRadius:16,padding:20,border:"1px solid #fde68a"}}>
          <div style={{fontWeight:800,fontSize:15,color:"#92400e",marginBottom:12}}>ðŸ“ˆ Areas to Improve</div>
          {improve.length === 0 && notStarted.length===0 ? (
            <div style={{color:"#6b7280",fontSize:13}}>Great job! Keep going.</div>
          ) : (
            <>
              {improve.map(s=>(
                <div key={s.id} style={{marginBottom:8,fontSize:13}}>
                  <div style={{fontWeight:600,color:"#92400e"}}>{s.icon} {s.name}</div>
                  <div style={{color:"#6b7280",fontSize:12}}>{s.pct}% complete{s.avgQuiz!==null?" Â· " + (s.avgQuiz) + "% quiz avg":""}. Consider retaking quizzes and reviewing flashcards.</div>
                </div>
              ))}
              {notStarted.length>0&&<div style={{marginTop:8,color:"#9ca3af",fontSize:12}}>Not started: {notStarted.map(s=>s.name).join(", ")}</div>}
            </>
          )}
        </div>
      </div>

      {/* Recommendations */}
      <div style={{background:"#fff",borderRadius:16,padding:20,boxShadow:"0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.06)",marginBottom:16}}>
        <div style={{fontWeight:800,fontSize:16,marginBottom:14}}>ðŸŽ¯ Personalized Recommendations</div>
        <div style={{display:"flex",flexDirection:"column",gap:10}}>
          {overallPct < 20 && (
            <div style={{background:"#eff6ff",borderRadius:10,padding:"12px 16px",fontSize:13}}>
              <strong>ðŸš€ Just getting started?</strong> Begin with Java Beginner or Mechanics Beginner lessons. They're designed to require no prior knowledge.
            </div>
          )}
          {overallPct >= 20 && overallPct < 60 && (
            <div style={{background:"#eff6ff",borderRadius:10,padding:"12px 16px",fontSize:13}}>
              <strong>ðŸ“š Keep the momentum!</strong> You're making solid progress. Focus on completing one subject before jumping to another â€” depth beats breadth early on.
            </div>
          )}
          {overallPct >= 60 && (
            <div style={{background:"#f0fdf4",borderRadius:10,padding:"12px 16px",fontSize:13}}>
              <strong>ðŸŒŸ Advanced learner!</strong> Consider exploring the Advanced lessons in your strongest subjects and contributing to the team forum.
            </div>
          )}
          {improve.map(s=>(
            <div key={s.id} style={{background:"#fffbeb",borderRadius:10,padding:"12px 16px",fontSize:13}}>
              <strong>{s.icon} Focus on {s.name}:</strong> Review intermediate lessons and use the {s.name} flashcard deck to reinforce key concepts.
              {s.avgQuiz!==null&&s.avgQuiz<70&&" Retake quizzes after reviewing notes to improve your score."}
            </div>
          ))}
          {Object.values(quizScores).length === 0 && (
            <div style={{background:"#fef2f2",borderRadius:10,padding:"12px 16px",fontSize:13}}>
              <strong>ðŸ§  Take some quizzes!</strong> Quizzes help identify gaps in your knowledge and unlock achievements. Try one after each subject.
            </div>
          )}
          {Object.values(flashProg).every(d=>Object.keys(d||{}).length===0) && (
            <div style={{background:"#f5f3ff",borderRadius:10,padding:"12px 16px",fontSize:13}}>
              <strong>ðŸƒ Try Flashcards!</strong> Spaced repetition is one of the most effective study methods. Start with the Java or Strategy deck.
            </div>
          )}
        </div>
      </div>

      {/* Quiz history */}
      {allQuizArr.length > 0 && (
        <div style={{background:"#fff",borderRadius:16,padding:20,boxShadow:"0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.06)"}}>
          <div style={{fontWeight:800,fontSize:16,marginBottom:14}}>ðŸ§  Quiz Score History</div>
          <div style={{display:"grid",gridTemplateColumns:"repeat(auto-fill,minmax(200px,1fr))",gap:10}}>
            {Object.entries(quizScores).map(([key,v])=>{
              const pct = Math.round(v.score/v.total*100);
              const [sub,lvl] = key.split("-");
              const subObj = SUBJECTS.find(s=>s.id===sub);
              return (
                <div key={key} style={{background:"#f8fafc",borderRadius:10,padding:"12px 14px",border:"1px solid #e2e8f0"}}>
                  <div style={{fontSize:11,color:"#94a3b8",textTransform:"uppercase",marginBottom:4}}>{subObj?.icon} {subObj?.name || sub} Â· {lvl}</div>
                  <div style={{display:"flex",alignItems:"center",gap:8}}>
